lessons.title: Project closeout & contract termination
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre o encerramento da obra, entrega final e os tipos de rescisão de contrato.
lessons.overview:
Every project has an end. The last phase is called closeout. At closeout, the team makes a punch list. This is a list of small outstanding items to fix before the client accepts the work. When the list is done, the client gives final acceptance and you do the handover.

Closeout has important documents and money steps. You deliver the as-built drawings, which show how the building was really made. The client then releases the retention and pays the final payment. After handover, the warranty period begins. For a Racional data center or hospital, a clean closeout protects the relationship and opens the door for the next project.

The contract can also end by termination. There are two types. For cause means one side broke the contract. For convenience means the client simply decides to stop, even when there is no problem. A good contract manager knows the difference and can talk about both calmly in English with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar o vocabulário de encerramento e entrega da obra. Frases-âncora: "We have a short punch list.", "Please sign off on the handover." e "Then you release the retention."

Frases curtas, na ordem dos passos: corrigir, aceitar, entregar, pagar.
lessons.situation: A obra está quase pronta. Na reunião final com o cliente americano, você apresenta a punch list, pede a aceitação e organiza a entrega e o pagamento final.
lessons.context: We are at closeout now. We have a short punch list with a few outstanding items. We will fix them this week. Then we ask for final acceptance and we do the handover. We will give you the as-built drawings. After that, please release the retention and the final payment.

lessons.title: Lessons learned with the client
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma reunião de lições aprendidas (lessons learned) com o cliente — destacando o que funcionou, o que pode melhorar e os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
At the end of a project, good teams stop and look back. This meeting is called lessons learned. The team talks about what went well and what they want to improve. The goal is simple: make the next project better. American clients like this meeting a lot. It is calm, honest, and looks to the future.

For a contract manager at Racional, this meeting matters every day. Racional builds offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and big data centers for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These clients come back for the next project. A clear lessons learned meeting shows that Racional learns and grows. It builds trust for the long term.

The tone is the key. We do not blame people. We talk about processes and the root cause of a problem. We start with the good news, then we share one area to improve, and we close with a clear next step. This way the client leaves the room with a good feeling and a plan for the future.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre a reunião de lessons learned (lições aprendidas), no fim do projeto com o cliente americano. O objetivo não é apontar culpados, e sim melhorar a próxima obra juntos.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "What went well was...", "One area to improve is..." e "Going forward, we will...". Comece pelo positivo, aponte a melhoria, e feche com um próximo passo concreto.
lessons.situation: Reunião de lições aprendidas com o representante do cliente, após a entrega de um data center. Você conduz a conversa de forma construtiva.
lessons.context: Let me share our lessons learned. What went well was the safety record. We had zero lost-time incidents. One area to improve is the response time on approvals. Going forward, we will set a clear deadline for each action item. Thank you for your feedback.

lessons.title: Construction industry overview: US vs. Brazil
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você compara a indústria da construção dos EUA e do Brasil em inglês simples — normas, materiais, mão de obra e fornecedores — para alinhar expectativas com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
The construction industry is not the same in every country. The rules, the materials, and the people are different. In the US, builders often use steel structure. In Brazil, we often use concrete. The building code and the fire code follow different standards. The workforce and the labor laws are different too. None of this is good or bad. It is just different.

For Racional, this is the heart of the work. American clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google bring habits from their home market. The contract manager must explain, in simple words, what is the same and what is different here. A good answer builds trust. The client sees that Racional knows the local market and respects the global standard.

This is called tropicalization. We take a global idea and we make it fit the Brazil context. We use a local supplier with a short lead time. We pick a cost-effective material. We always comply with the local code. The result is a building that works here, with the same quality the client expects.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE. O cliente americano traz expectativas do mercado dele. Saber explicar, em inglês simples, o que é igual e o que é diferente no Brasil evita ruído e mostra domínio.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "In the US, you usually...; in Brazil, we usually..." e "It is similar, but different."
lessons.situation: Visita técnica com o cliente americano. Ele pergunta por que o projeto usa concreto, e não estrutura metálica como nos EUA.
lessons.context: In the US, you usually build with steel structure. In Brazil, we often use concrete. It is local and cost-effective. It fits our labor laws and our fire code. It is similar, but different. The standard is high in both countries. Let me explain why concrete works here.

lessons.title: Project lifecycle (design — build — handover)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve o ciclo de vida do projeto em inglês — do design à entrega — citando fases, marcos e se a obra está no prazo.
lessons.overview:
Every building follows the same path. We call it the project lifecycle. First comes the design phase, when the project is on paper. Then comes the construction phase, when the team builds. At the end comes the handover, when we give the building to the client. Each step has a name, and each step has a milestone — a key date that we must hit.

For Racional, this path is the same for every segment — offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers. The construction phase has clear steps: foundations, then the structure, then MEP (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing), then the façade, then the finishes, and at the end the commissioning. The contract manager follows each phase and reports the status to the client.

American clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google ask one question all the time: are we on schedule? A clear answer builds trust. When you can walk through each phase in simple English and say what is planned for next month, the client feels safe. This lesson gives you the words to do that.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre o project lifecycle (ciclo de vida do projeto). Você vai nomear as fases e dizer se a obra está no prazo.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "We are now in the structure phase.", "We are on schedule." e "Let me walk you through the next milestone."
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de status. O cliente americano quer entender em que fase a obra está e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.context: Let me walk you through the project lifecycle. The design phase is done. We are now in the construction phase. The foundations are ready and the structure is up. MEP and the façade come next. We are on schedule. The next milestone is planned for July.

lessons.title: Music talk 2: Sade — British soul & timeless artists
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre música com o cliente — descrevendo o estilo de uma artista como Sade — para criar conexão e rapport.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. When a meeting ends, the small talk begins. People talk about food, travel, and music. A short, warm chat about a favorite artist builds rapport. It shows the human side. American clients enjoy this kind of easy conversation a lot.

This lesson is about Sade, a British singer with a smooth and soulful voice. Her music is mellow and timeless — it never gets old. People play it as background music at home or in a café. You can say her songs remind you of a special time. Words like these help you talk about music in simple English.

For a contract manager at Racional, these small moments matter. A project with a client like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google lasts 18 to 24 months. That is a long time. A warm chat about a song you both love builds a bond that helps in every meeting. Business is built on numbers, but trust is built on these human moments.

lessons.title: Site selection & feasibility studies
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala em inglês sobre escolha de terreno e estudo de viabilidade — acessos, infraestrutura, energia, solo e riscos — com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before we build, we choose the place. This is called site selection. Then we study the place to see if the project can work. This is the feasibility study. We look at the access roads, the local infrastructure, the power supply, and the soil conditions. We also check the zoning rules. The goal is one answer: is this site viable or not?

For Racional, this step is critical, above all for data centers. A data center for a client like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google needs a lot of power and good network access. The team must assess each site and weigh every trade-off. A good study finds the risk early, when it is cheap to fix. A bad study finds it late, when it is very expensive.

The contract manager must explain this study to the client in clear English. The site must meet the requirements of the project. When you can say why a site is viable — strong power, good access, firm soil — the client trusts the decision. This lesson gives you the words to lead that conversation.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre site selection (escolha do terreno) e feasibility study (estudo de viabilidade).

Relembre as frases-âncora: "We need to assess the site.", "The site is viable." e "It meets the requirements."
lessons.situation: Reunião inicial com o cliente americano sobre um possível terreno para um novo data center. Você apresenta os pontos do estudo de viabilidade.
lessons.context: Let me share the feasibility study. The site has good access and strong power supply. The soil conditions are firm. The zoning is fine. There is one risk: the location is far from the city. We need to assess this trade-off. In the end, the site is viable and meets the requirements.

lessons.title: Geotechnical & soil investigation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala em inglês sobre investigação do solo — sondagem, amostras, capacidade de carga e nível d'água — para alinhar a fundação com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before we design the foundations, we must know the ground. This is the soil investigation, also called a geotechnical survey. The team drills a borehole and takes a sample of the soil. Then they write a soil report. The report shows the bearing capacity — how much weight the ground can hold — and the level of the water table.

For Racional, this step is the base of every project, in every segment. A heavy data center for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google needs strong ground. If the soil is soft soil, the building can settle and crack. If the soil is firm soil or bedrock, the foundation is simple and safe. The right answer comes only from a good survey.

The contract manager must read the soil report and explain it to the client in clear English. A bad surprise in the ground is very expensive to fix later. When you know the site conditions early, you protect the schedule and the budget. This lesson gives you the words to discuss the soil with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre soil investigation (investigação do solo) e geotechnical survey (sondagem geotécnica).

Relembre as frases-âncora: "We drill a borehole and take a sample.", "The soil report shows the bearing capacity." e "The soil is firm."
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o cliente americano sobre a fundação. Você apresenta os resultados da sondagem do solo.
lessons.context: Let me share the soil report. We drilled three boreholes and took samples. The soil is firm and the bearing capacity is good. The water table is low. The site conditions are safe for our foundation. There is no soft soil here.

lessons.title: Foundations (deep, shallow, special)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você nomeia e diferencia os três grandes grupos de fundação — rasa, profunda e especial — em inglês simples, para explicar ao cliente norte-americano qual solução a obra vai usar e por quê.
lessons.overview:
Every building starts with the foundation. The foundation is the part under the ground. It takes the weight of the building. We call this weight the load. The foundation must carry the load to the soil. If the foundation is good, the building is safe and strong.

There are three big groups. A shallow foundation is near ground level. We use it on firm soil. A deep foundation goes down many meters. We use it on soft soil. Here we use piles to reach the strong rock. A special foundation is for hard cases, like a diaphragm wall in a deep basement.

At Racional, the soil is different on every site. A hospital, a shopping center, or a hyperscale data center for Microsoft or Amazon all need the right foundation. The contract manager must explain this choice in clear English. The client wants to know: firm soil or soft soil? Shallow or deep? This is the first step of a safe project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a lógica que liga solo e fundação: "We use shallow foundations on firm soil." e "For soft soil, we use deep foundations."

Lembre também da ideia central: "The foundation carries the load to the soil." (A fundação leva a carga ao solo.) Solo firme → rasa. Solo mole → profunda.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de projeto de um hospital, o cliente norte-americano quer entender qual fundação a obra vai adotar. Você explica a escolha ligando-a sempre ao solo.
lessons.context: The foundation carries the load to the soil. The soil here is soft, so we use deep foundations. We drive piles down to the rock. Near the gate, the soil is firm. There we use shallow footings. This is safe and strong.

lessons.title: Structural systems: concrete vs. steel
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você compara estrutura de concreto e estrutura de aço em inglês simples, citando vantagens de cada uma para recomendar a melhor opção ao cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
The structural system is the skeleton of the building. It holds the floors and the roof. There are two main choices. The first is a concrete structure. The second is a steel structure. Both use columns and beams. The space between two columns is the span.

Each system has good points. A steel frame is lightweight and faster to erect. So a steel building can be faster to build. A reinforced concrete structure has better fire resistance and can be more cost-effective in Brazil. This choice is a real trade-off. The contract manager must explain it well.

At Racional, this choice happens on every project. A hyperscale data center for Google may favor steel for speed. A hospital may favor concrete for fire resistance and cost. When you meet the North American client, you recommend the right system. You give clear reasons. This builds trust and a strong project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases para comparar e recomendar: "Steel is faster to build, but concrete is more cost-effective here."

Lembre da estrutura para recomendar: "I recommend a concrete structure for this project." e do termo-chave trade-off (escolha com prós e contras).
lessons.situation: O cliente norte-americano de um data center pergunta se a obra será em concreto ou aço. Você compara os dois e recomenda o melhor para o caso.
lessons.context: We have two options: a concrete structure or a steel structure. Steel is lightweight and faster to erect, so it is faster to build. Concrete has better fire resistance and is more cost-effective here. It is a trade-off. For this data center, I recommend steel.

lessons.title: Geopolitics: war, trade & global affairs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de notícias e temas globais com o cliente norte-americano de forma leve e neutra, mantendo a conversa profissional sem entrar em polêmica.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the client wants to talk about the news. This is small talk. He may talk about global affairs: trade, a tariff, or the supply chain. Many North American clients follow the news every day. To connect with them, you can talk a little about these topics.

But this is a sensitive area. A conflict or a war is a complex situation. It is smart to stay neutral. You do not need to pick a side. You can listen and say a few words. A good question is: "What's your take?" This shows interest. Then you can change the subject back to the project.

For Racional, the client is often from the United States. Global news can have an impact on business: a tariff can change the price of steel; the supply chain can change the lead time of a part. You do not need strong opinions. You just need to listen, stay polite, and keep an eye on the topics that touch the project.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de relacionamento. O foco é conexão, não técnica. Retome a pergunta leve: "What's your take?" (Qual a sua opinião?).

Lembre também de como manter o tom neutro: "It's a complex situation. I try to stay neutral." e como voltar ao trabalho: "Anyway, let's go back to the project."
lessons.situation: No café antes da reunião, o cliente norte-americano comenta uma notícia de comércio internacional. Você responde de forma leve, neutra e simpática.
lessons.context: Client: Did you see the news about the new tariff? It can change steel prices. What's your take? You: It's a complex situation. I try to stay neutral. But yes, we keep an eye on it. It can have an impact on our supply chain. Anyway, let's go back to the project.

lessons.title: Tropicalização 1: structural choice — Brazil vs. US
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao cliente norte-americano por que a escolha estrutural no Brasil pode ser diferente da dos EUA, usando inglês simples para alinhar expectativas sobre concreto e aço.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, a steel structure is often the default choice. It is common practice there. But in Brazil, the equation is different. The material cost is different. The local labor is different. Here, concrete is often the best value. This is called tropicalization.

Why does the choice change? In Brazil, the local market has a strong concrete supply. The skilled workforce for concrete is large. So concrete can make sense and be a good fit. In the US, steel fabrication and supply availability are strong, so steel can win. The same project, two countries, two answers.

For Racional, this is a key point with the North American client. The client may expect steel, because that is normal at home. The contract manager must align expectations early. You explain: "The equation is different here." You show that concrete can be the right fit for Brazil. This avoids surprises and builds a strong, honest relationship.
lessons.intro:
O foco é alinhar expectativas: o que é padrão nos EUA pode não ser o melhor no Brasil. Retome a frase-âncora: "In the US, steel is the default. But here, the equation is different."

Lembre também de: "In Brazil, concrete is often the best value." e "Let me align expectations."
lessons.situation: O cliente norte-americano de um escritório esperava aço, como é padrão nos EUA. Você explica, com calma, por que no Brasil o concreto pode ser a melhor escolha.
lessons.context: In the US, steel is the default choice. It is common practice there. But in Brazil, the equation is different. The material cost and the local labor are different. Here, concrete is often the best value. Let me align expectations: for this project, concrete is the right fit.

lessons.title: Reinforced concrete in detail
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve as etapas do concreto armado em inglês simples — fôrma, armadura, lançamento e cura — para acompanhar a execução e reportar o avanço ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Reinforced concrete is concrete with steel inside. The steel bars are the rebar. The rebar gives the concrete strength. This is the most common structure in Brazil. Every contract manager must know its steps.

First, the team builds the formwork. This is the mold. Then they place the rebar inside. Next, they pour the concrete and vibrate it to remove air. After some hours, the concrete starts to set. Then it must cure for days to reach full compressive strength. Finally, the team can strip the formwork. We often use ready-mix concrete from a truck and a concrete pump to move it.

At Racional, this happens on almost every slab and column. On a hospital or a shopping center, quality control is key. We do a slump test to check the concrete mix. When you report to the client, you use these words: pour, cure, strength. Clear words show control and a safe project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a sequência do concreto: "We build the formwork, place the rebar, and pour the concrete."

Lembre também das etapas finais: "The concrete needs time to cure." e "Then we strip the formwork."

lessons.title: Structural steel & prefabrication
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve o uso de estrutura metálica e pré-fabricação em inglês simples — fabricação fora da obra, montagem com guindaste e ganho de prazo — para reportar o avanço ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Structural steel is a fast way to build. The big idea is prefabrication. We make the steel parts in a fabrication shop, far from the site. This is off-site work. Then we bring the parts to the site. There we put them together. This is on-site work.

The parts are the steel beam and the steel column. We join them with a connection. Some connections use a bolt: we bolt the parts. Others use a weld. On site, a crane helps us lift the heavy parts. This is the steel erection. It is fast and clean.

For Racional, prefabrication brings a big schedule gain. A hyperscale data center for Amazon or Microsoft needs speed. With steel, we build off-site while the foundation cures on-site. Both jobs happen at the same time. When you report to the client, you can show this gain. Faster steel erection means an earlier handover. The client likes that.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a lógica da pré-fabricação: "We make the parts off-site, then we erect them on-site."

Lembre do ganho de prazo: "Steel gives us a schedule gain." e da montagem: "The crane lifts the steel beams."
lessons.situation: O cliente norte-americano do data center quer acelerar a obra. Você explica como a estrutura metálica pré-fabricada traz ganho de prazo.
lessons.context: We use structural steel for speed. We make the parts off-site, in the fabrication shop. Then we bring them on-site. The crane lifts the steel beams and columns. We bolt the connections. This steel erection gives us a real schedule gain.

lessons.title: Formwork, shoring & temporary works
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, os trabalhos temporários da estrutura — fôrma, escoramento e cimbramento — e diz com clareza ao cliente quando a fôrma pode sair e por que é seguro.
lessons.overview:
Every concrete structure starts with temporary works. The formwork is the mold for the wet concrete. The shoring holds the slab from below. These parts are not part of the final building, but the building cannot rise without them. At Racional, this happens on every project, from offices to hospitals to large data centers.

Temporary works are also safety works. Fresh concrete is weak. It needs time to cure and reach strength. If the shoring is bad, the slab can collapse. So the contract manager must watch the schedule and the load with great care. A clear plan keeps the team safe and keeps the project on time.

American clients always ask two simple questions on site: "Is it safe?" and "When can we strip the formwork?" A good answer joins the schedule and the safety in one sentence. This is daily language for a Racional contract manager, and clear English here builds trust with the client.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), do coração técnico do programa. O tema são os trabalhos temporários — fôrma, escoramento e cimbramento.

Duas frases-âncora para a prática:
"We can strip the formwork after the concrete reaches strength." (Podemos desformar depois que o concreto atinge a resistência.)
"The shoring supports the slab, and it is safe." (O escoramento sustenta a laje, e está seguro.)
lessons.situation: Visita de obra com o cliente americano. Vocês estão diante de uma laje recém-concretada, ainda escorada, e ele pergunta quando a fôrma pode sair.
lessons.context: This slab was poured on Monday. The formwork stays in place now. The shoring carries the load from below. The concrete needs more days to reach strength. We can strip the formwork next week, and it is fully safe.

lessons.title: Family trips & vacation stories
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta, em inglês simples, uma história curta de viagem em família ou férias e devolve a pergunta ao cliente americano para manter a conversa.
lessons.overview:
A big project at Racional can last 18 to 24 months. In that time, the American client becomes almost a colleague. Between formal meetings, people talk about real life. A family trip, a long weekend, or time at the beach are easy and warm topics. This small talk builds a real human bond.

Personal stories are powerful because they are honest. When you say the kids loved the trip, or that a few days off helped you recharge, the client sees the person behind the contract manager. This trust is useful later, in hard meetings about schedule or cost.

The goal here is simple. Tell a short and friendly story, and then return the question. Small talk is an exchange, not a long speech. A line like "How about you? Any travel plans?" keeps the conversation alive and shows you care about the other person too.

lessons.title: MEP overview (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês simples, a visão geral de MEP — sistemas mecânicos, elétricos e hidráulicos — e explica como você coordena os três para evitar interferências na obra.
lessons.overview:
MEP means three systems: mechanical, electrical and plumbing. Mechanical is air conditioning and ventilation. Electrical is power and panels. Plumbing is water and drainage. In offices, hospitals and data centers, these systems are the heart of the building. For a data center client like Microsoft or Amazon, MEP is the whole project.

The three systems share the same ceiling space. They cannot use the same place at the same time. When two systems hit the same spot, this is a clash. A clash on site means rework, delay and extra cost. So the team uses a 3D model to find clashes early, before installation.

For a Racional contract manager, the main job in MEP is not to install each system. The job is coordination. You make the three disciplines and their subcontractors work together. Clear English in these coordination meetings helps you avoid clashes and keep the schedule safe.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). MEP é um dos vocabulários mais importantes para você, sobretudo em data centers e hospitais.

"We coordinate the systems to avoid clashes." (Coordenamos os sistemas para evitar interferências.)

lessons.title: Mechanical systems & HVAC
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre os sistemas mecânicos e o HVAC — ar-condicionado, ventilação e resfriamento — e explica a importância da capacidade de resfriamento para o cliente.
lessons.overview:
The mechanical system controls the air inside a building. The short name is HVAC: heating, ventilation and air conditioning. It keeps the air clean, the temperature right and the rooms comfortable. In a hospital or an office, this means comfort. In a data center, this means survival.

A data center has many machines, and machines make a lot of heat. This heat is the heat load. The HVAC must remove it all day and all night. A chiller makes cold water for cooling. Ducts carry the cold air to each room. If the cooling capacity is too small, the machines get too hot and stop.

For clients like Microsoft, Amazon or Google, cooling is the number one topic. They ask about temperature, airflow and backup. A Racional contract manager must explain the HVAC plan in clear and simple English. When you say the system keeps the rooms cool day and night, the client feels safe.

Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). O tema são os sistemas mecânicos e o HVAC — central em data centers, onde resfriar é o assunto número um.

lessons.title: Electrical systems & substations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre o sistema elétrico e as subestações — fornecimento de energia, painéis, gerador de backup e redundância — e explica ao cliente como a energia chega segura ao prédio.
lessons.overview:
The electrical system brings power to the whole building. Power comes from the grid and enters through a substation. The substation lowers the voltage to a safe level. Then the switchgear and the panels distribute power to every floor and every room. Without power, nothing works.

In a hospital or a data center, power can never stop. A power cut is a serious risk. So the design uses a backup generator and redundancy. Redundancy means there is always a second path for the power. If one path fails, the other keeps the building alive. This is why data center clients ask so many questions about power.

For a Racional contract manager, the electrical system is a top priority. Clients like Microsoft and Amazon want to know about the power supply, the backup and the risk of an outage. Clear and simple English helps you explain that the design is safe and has no single point of failure.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). O tema é o sistema elétrico e as subestações — crítico em hospitais e data centers, onde a energia não pode parar.

lessons.title: Plumbing & hydraulics
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre o sistema hidráulico — abastecimento de água, tubos, válvulas, drenagem e testes de pressão — e explica ao cliente que tudo está testado antes de fechar as paredes.
lessons.overview:
The plumbing system moves water through the building. The water supply brings clean water in. Pipes carry the water, and valves open and close the flow. The drainage takes used water and sewage out. In offices, hospitals and shopping centers, this system serves people every day.

The biggest risk in plumbing is a leak. A small leak inside a wall can cause big damage later. So the team runs a pressure test on every pipe. If the water pressure stays stable, there is no leak. This test happens before the team closes the walls, because a leak behind a finished wall is very hard and costly to fix.

For a Racional contract manager, the rule is simple and strong: test first, close the walls later. American clients value this discipline. When you explain in clear English that every pipe passed the pressure test before the walls were closed, the client trusts your quality control.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). O tema é o sistema hidráulico — tubos, válvulas, drenagem e, acima de tudo, o teste de pressão antes de fechar as paredes.

lessons.title: American humor, idioms & slang
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai entender gírias, expressões (idioms) e o humor do cliente americano e responder com leveza, sem se perder na conversa.
lessons.overview:
American clients talk in a friendly way. They use slang and idioms every day. An idiom is a phrase with a hidden meaning. "It's a piece of cake" does not talk about cake. It means something is very easy. You hear these phrases on the job site and in meetings.

American humor is often light. People make jokes about themselves. They use sarcasm too. You do not need to make jokes. You only need to understand and smile. This helps you build trust with the client. At Racional, your clients are from the United States. They run big projects like offices, hospitals, and data centers for Microsoft, Amazon, and Google.

When you understand slang, the talk feels easy. You can say "no worries" or "let's wrap up." If you do not understand a word, you can ask: "What does that mean?" Americans like to explain. This small question makes the relationship stronger and warmer.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE (Módulo M6), de repertório cultural. O foco é entender o cliente americano quando ele usa gírias e idioms.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "It's a piece of cake" (é muito fácil), "Let's touch base tomorrow" (vamos nos alinhar amanhã) e "We're on the same page" (estamos alinhados). E a regra de ouro: se não entendeu, pergunte "What does that mean?"
lessons.situation: Fim de um dia puxado de obra. O cliente americano relaxa, solta algumas gírias e faz uma piada leve. Você acompanha o clima.
lessons.context: Good work today. That was a piece of cake for your team. Let's call it a day. We can touch base tomorrow. I think we are on the same page on the schedule. No worries about the rest.

lessons.title: Fire protection systems
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai descrever os sistemas de proteção contra incêndio de uma obra (sprinklers, bomba, alarme) em inglês simples, com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Every building needs a fire protection system. This system keeps people safe. It has two parts. Active protection uses water and alarms to fight a fire. Passive protection uses walls and doors to stop the fire and smoke. Both parts work together.

The active system has sprinklers, a fire pump, and a fire alarm. A smoke detector finds smoke fast. Then the sprinklers start and the pump pushes water through the pipes. The passive system has fire doors and fireproofing on the steel. A fire compartment holds the fire in one area.

At Racional, fire protection is very important. Hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers for Amazon, Microsoft, and Google all need strong systems. The American client asks many questions about this. You must talk about sprinklers, pumps, and the fire rating of each part. Clear words here build trust and keep the project safe.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), o coração técnico. Foco: o sistema de proteção contra incêndio.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "The system has sprinklers and a fire pump" (o sistema tem sprinklers e bomba), "The smoke detector starts the alarm" (o detector aciona o alarme) e "We test the fire pump every month" (testamos a bomba todo mês).
lessons.situation: Visita do cliente americano à obra de um data center. Ele pergunta como funciona a proteção contra incêndio do prédio.
lessons.context: Our building has a full fire protection system. The smoke detector finds smoke fast. Then the alarm starts. The sprinklers open and the fire pump pushes water. Fire doors stop the smoke. We test the pump every month.

vocab.example: The building has a fire protection system.

lessons.title: Tropicalização 2: fire code — corpo de bombeiros (BR)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai explicar ao cliente americano por que o projeto de incêndio segue o corpo de bombeiros (fire code) brasileiro e como obtemos a aprovação.
lessons.overview:
In Brazil, the fire department controls fire safety. They make the rules. We call these rules the fire code. Every building must follow this code. The team makes a fire project and sends it to the fire department. This is part of "tropicalização": we adapt the American design to the Brazilian rules.

The fire department checks the project. Then they do a fire inspection on the site. If everything is right, they give the operating permit. Without this permit, the building cannot open. So we must comply with every code requirement. If they find a problem, they write a finding, and we fix it.

This is very important for Racional. The American client knows the rules from the United States. But Brazil is different. The Brazilian standard can differ from the American one. Your job is to bridge the gap. You explain the local rules in simple English. This keeps the project legal and on time for offices, hospitals, and data centers.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), de tropicalização. Foco: o fire code brasileiro e o corpo de bombeiros.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "We must comply with the local fire code" (precisamos seguir o código local), "The fire department gives the operating permit" (o corpo de bombeiros dá a licença de funcionamento) e "The Brazilian standard differs from the American one" (a norma brasileira difere da americana).
lessons.situation: Reunião com o cliente americano. Ele estranha o processo de incêndio do Brasil e você explica como funciona o corpo de bombeiros.
lessons.context: In Brazil, the fire department makes the rules. We must comply with the local fire code. We send a fire project to them. They do an inspection on site. Then they give the operating permit. Without it, the building cannot open.

lessons.title: Building envelope & facade
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai descrever a fachada e o envelope do prédio (curtain wall, vidro, vedação) e falar de testes de estanqueidade com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
The building envelope is the skin of the building. It is the wall between the inside and the outside. The facade is the front face that people see. A good envelope keeps the rain, the heat, and the noise outside. It protects the people inside.

Many buildings use a curtain wall. This is a light wall of glazing (glass) and metal. The mullion holds the glass. Other buildings use cladding on the wall. We add sealant for weatherproofing. We also test for airtightness and good thermal performance, so the building saves energy.

For Racional, the facade is very important. Office towers and data centers for Microsoft and Amazon need a strong, clean envelope. Before we install all the glass, we build a mock-up. Then we do a water test. If we find a leak, we fix it first. This protects the client and keeps the project on schedule.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), técnica. Foco: o envelope e a fachada do prédio.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "The curtain wall has glass and metal" (o curtain wall tem vidro e metal), "We do a water test on the mock-up" (fazemos teste de água no protótipo) e "There is no leak" (não há vazamento).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano visita a obra de uma torre de escritórios e quer entender como a fachada de vidro é testada.
lessons.context: The facade is the skin of the building. We use a curtain wall with glass and metal. First we build a mock-up. Then we do a water test. We check for leaks. We add sealant for weatherproofing. The building stays dry inside.

lessons.title: Vertical transportation (elevators, traffic study)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar sobre transporte vertical (elevadores, escadas rolantes, estudo de tráfego) e tempo de espera com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Vertical transportation moves people up and down the building. The main parts are the elevator and the escalator. In a tall office tower or a hospital, this is very important. People do not like to wait. A long waiting time makes the client unhappy.

Before we choose the elevators, we do a traffic study. This study looks at the peak hour, when many people arrive at the same time. It checks the capacity and the speed of each car. The elevator car goes up and down inside the hoistway. The machine room holds the motor. We want a fast and smooth ride.

For Racional, this is key in big projects. Office towers and shopping centers for American clients need elevators that handle heavy traffic. At the end, we do the commissioning. We test every car and check the waiting time. A good system makes the building work well and keeps the client happy.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), técnica. Foco: transporte vertical e estudo de tráfego.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "We do a traffic study first" (fazemos o estudo de tráfego antes), "The waiting time is short" (o tempo de espera é curto) e "The elevator has a smooth ride" (o elevador tem viagem suave).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pergunta como os elevadores da torre vão aguentar o horário de pico com muita gente.
lessons.context: Vertical transportation moves people up and down. First we do a traffic study. It checks the peak hour. We look at the capacity and the speed of each car. We want a short waiting time and a smooth ride. Then we do the commissioning.

lessons.title: Music talk 3: Lenny Kravitz — rock, funk & guitar legends
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conversar sobre música — rock, funk e Lenny Kravitz — para criar conexão e rapport com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. This is a Music Talk lesson. Today the artist is Lenny Kravitz. He is an American singer and a famous guitar player. He mixes rock and funk. His songs have a strong groove and a great vibe.

When you talk about music, the client relaxes. You can say a band has a good riff or a great guitar solo. You can talk about a favorite album or a big hit. You do not need hard words. Simple sentences work very well: "I love this song" or "This album is unforgettable."

For Racional, this matters a lot. A project with an American client can take 18 to 24 months. You meet the client many times. Small talk about music builds a long and warm relationship. Lenny Kravitz is a safe and fun topic. It helps you go from a work talk to a real human connection.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE (Módulo M5), da trilha Music Talk. Foco: conversar sobre música para criar rapport.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "I love this song" (eu amo essa música), "He is a great guitar player" (ele é um ótimo guitarrista) e "This album is unforgettable" (esse álbum é inesquecível).
lessons.situation: Pausa do café com o cliente americano. Sai uma música do Lenny Kravitz e vocês começam a conversar sobre rock e funk.

lessons.title: Architectural finishes
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre acabamentos arquitetônicos e padrão de entrega em uma reunião de obra com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Architectural finishes are the last layer of a building. They are the parts people see and touch every day: the flooring, the ceiling, the paint, the doors and frames, and the tile in the bathrooms. The structure holds the building up, but the finishes give the building its quality and its look. For a Racional client, the finishes are the first thing they notice when they walk in.

Finishes are very important for the contract manager. The finish schedule is a list that shows the material for each room. It tells you which flooring, which paint, and which tile to use. Good workmanship means the work is clean and well done. On a corporate office for an American client, the level of finish must be high, because the client will use that space for important meetings.

Many Racional projects start with a model floor. This is one floor finished first, so the client can see and approve the quality. After the client approves the sample and the model floor, the team builds all the other floors to match it. Small problems happen, so the team does touch-up work at the end. Clear talk about finishes keeps the client happy and protects the final delivery.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar dos acabamentos e do padrão de entrega com o cliente americano. Frases-âncora: "This is the finish schedule for the model floor.", "The new floors will match the sample." e "We will do the touch-up before delivery."

Use frases curtas, uma ideia por frase. Aponte para o material e diga o nome em inglês.
lessons.situation: Você está mostrando o pavimento-modelo (model floor) ao representante do cliente americano. Ele quer confirmar o padrão de acabamento antes de liberar os outros andares.
lessons.context: This is the model floor. Here you can see the finishes. The flooring is ready and the paint is done. The doors and frames are new. This is the finish schedule for this floor. The other floors will match this sample. We will do a small touch-up before we hand over the floor. The workmanship is clean and the level of finish is high.

lessons.title: Office towers & corporate buildings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre torres de escritórios, área e eficiência de planta para um cliente corporativo.
lessons.overview:
An office tower is a tall corporate building with many floors. Big companies rent space in these towers for their teams. Racional builds high-quality office towers for important clients in São Paulo and other cities. Each floor must be ready for work, with good light, good air, and a clean look.

Two numbers matter a lot in an office tower. The first is the gross area, which is the total area of the floor. The second is the net leasable area, which is the area the company can really use and pay for. The relation between them is the efficiency. A good floor plate with a small core gives more usable space, so the client is happy. An open floor plan also helps teams work together.

Many American clients want a Class A building with LEED certification. Class A means top quality. LEED means the building is green and saves energy. These features help the client find a good tenant and lease the space fast. When Racional can target high efficiency and a strong certification, the project has more value for everyone.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar de área, eficiência e padrão de um edifício corporativo. Frases-âncora: "This floor has high efficiency.", "The core is small, so the net area is large." e "This is a Class A building with LEED certification."

Use frases curtas e números simples. Uma ideia por frase.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta um andar da torre corporativa a um cliente americano. Ele quer entender a eficiência da planta e o padrão do edifício antes de fechar a locação.
lessons.context: Welcome to our office tower. This is a Class A building. The gross area of this floor is large. The core is small, so the net leasable area is high. This gives us good efficiency. We have an open floor plan for your teams. The building also has LEED certification. You can lease this floor and start fast.

lessons.title: Hospital construction & healthcare facilities
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre construção de hospitais, sistemas críticos e segurança do paciente.
lessons.overview:
A healthcare facility is one of the hardest projects to build. A hospital is never just a building. It is a place where doctors save lives every day. The operating room and the ICU must work all the time. For Racional, a hospital project means very high quality and zero room for error.

The most important word in a hospital is safety. Patient safety comes first. Many systems are critical systems: they cannot stop. So the hospital has redundancy. This means we have a backup for every important part. If one power feed stops, a backup generator starts in seconds. The goal is high uptime, so the hospital does not fail.

A hospital also has special systems that other buildings do not have. There is medical gas for the patients. There is strong air filtration for infection control, to keep the air clean. All these systems must stay running during surgery. When Racional explains this to an American client, clear and simple English about safety builds trust fast.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar de sistemas críticos e segurança do paciente em um hospital. Frases-âncora: "Patient safety comes first.", "These systems must stay running." e "We have redundancy and a backup generator."

Use frases curtas e firmes. Em hospital, o tom é de segurança e confiança.
lessons.situation: Você acompanha o cliente americano em uma visita à obra de um hospital. Ele pergunta como você garante que os sistemas críticos não vão parar.
lessons.context: This is the operating room and this is the ICU. These are critical systems. They must stay running all the time. Patient safety comes first. We have redundancy here. If one power feed fails, the backup generator starts in seconds. We also have medical gas and strong air filtration for infection control. Our goal is high uptime.

lessons.title: Shopping centers & retail
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre shopping centers, lojas, fit-out e a abertura ao público.
lessons.overview:
A shopping center, or mall, is a large retail building with many stores. People go there to shop, to eat, and to spend time with family. Racional builds malls with a strong common area, a food court, and a large parking structure. The goal is to bring people in and keep them happy.

One key word is the anchor store. This is a big, famous store that pulls many people into the mall. More people means more footfall, and more footfall is good for every tenant. Each tenant gets an empty space and does the fit-out, which means they build their own store inside. The storefront is the front of the store, the part the client sees.

A mall has a hard schedule. The most important date is the grand opening, the day the mall opens to the public. To hit this date, Racional uses phasing: the team builds and opens the mall in parts. The contract manager must show the client that the project is on track and that Racional will hand over each area on time. A clean handover makes the grand opening a success.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar do shopping, das lojas e da abertura ao público. Frases-âncora: "The anchor store brings more footfall.", "The project is on track for the grand opening." e "We will hand over this area on time."

lessons.context: Welcome to our shopping center. This is the common area and this is the food court. The anchor store is here. It will bring a lot of footfall. Each tenant will do the fit-out of their store. The project is on track for the grand opening. We use phasing, so we open the mall in parts. We will hand over this area on time.

lessons.title: American sports (NFL, NBA, MLB, golf)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber conversar, em inglês simples, sobre esportes americanos para criar conexão com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, sports are everywhere. American people love to talk about their team. They watch games on TV with family and friends. For a Racional contract manager, a short talk about sports is a great way to break the ice with an American client and build a real connection.

The big sports are easy to know. Football (American football) is number one, and the biggest game is the Super Bowl. Basketball (the NBA) and baseball (the MLB) are also very popular. Golf is the sport for business: many deals start when two people play a round of golf together. Be careful: in the US, "football" means American football, and "soccer" means the game we call futebol in Brazil.

You do not need to be an expert. You just need a few simple phrases. You can ask, "Did you catch the game last night?" or "Who do you root for?" You can talk about the score, the playoffs, or a close game. A short, friendly talk before a meeting makes the American client feel at home and helps the long Racional project run more smoothly.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar small talk sobre esportes para abrir uma conversa com o cliente americano. Frases-âncora: "Did you catch the game last night?", "Who do you root for?" e "It was a close game!"

Tom leve e amigável. Não precisa ser especialista, só puxar conversa.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, você quer quebrar o gelo com o cliente americano. Você sabe que ele gosta de futebol americano e que houve um jogo importante na noite anterior.
lessons.context: Hi! Did you catch the game last night? It was a close game! I like football too. Who do you root for? My team is not in the playoffs this year. Do you play golf? We can play a round of golf one day. I am a big fan of sports. The score was very close at the end.

lessons.title: Data centers (cooling, redundancy, Tier)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre data centers, resfriamento, redundância e Tier para clientes como Microsoft, Amazon e Google.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a building full of computers, called servers. These servers run the internet, the cloud, and big software. Racional builds hyperscale data centers for the largest clients in the world, like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. Hyperscale means very, very large. This is one of the most important segments for Racional today.

A data center must never stop. The most important word is uptime. If the data center has downtime, the client loses a lot of money. So the building has a lot of redundancy. Engineers talk about N+1 or 2N: this means extra equipment, so there is always a backup. The UPS and the generators keep the power on if the city power goes down. They take over in seconds.

The servers make a lot of heat, so a strong cooling system is key. If the room gets too hot, the servers overheat and stop. The server room, also called white space, has a raised floor for cables and cold air. The load is the power the servers use. Clients also ask about the Tier level, like Tier III or Tier IV. A higher Tier means more safety and more uptime. Clear English about these systems is a must for the Racional contract manager.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar de resfriamento, redundância e Tier em um data center. Frases-âncora: "The cooling system keeps the servers cool.", "We have redundancy, so the system never goes down." e "This is a Tier IV data center."

Use frases curtas e termos técnicos simples. Uma ideia por frase.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a obra de um data center hyperscale ao cliente americano (Microsoft, Amazon ou Google). Ele quer entender a redundância e o sistema de resfriamento.
lessons.context: This is a hyperscale data center. This is the server room, the white space. It has a raised floor for the cables and the cold air. The cooling system keeps the servers cool, so they do not overheat. We have a lot of redundancy here. This is a Tier IV building. If the city power goes down, the generators take over in seconds. Our goal is very high uptime.

vocab.example: This data center is very large.

lessons.title: Industrial facilities & manufacturing plants
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, uma obra industrial — galpão, linha de produção, layout e fluxo de materiais — para conversar com o cliente sobre manufacturing plants.
lessons.overview:
An industrial facility is a building made for work and production. A manufacturing plant makes products. A warehouse stores them. These buildings look simple, but they are not. The floor must be very strong. The clear height must be high. The space must be open and flexible.

At Racional, industry is a key segment. We build big plants and large warehouses. We also build data centers for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These projects need a strong industrial floor, a clear layout, and good material flow. The building must support heavy machines and trucks every day.

As a contract manager, you talk about these things with the client. You explain the building shell, the loading dock, and the production line. You use simple words to describe a complex building. This lesson gives you the basic vocabulary to do that with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai usar frases-âncora simples para descrever a obra industrial: "This is a manufacturing plant.", "The floor is heavy-duty." e "The layout keeps the material flow clear."

lessons.title: Procurement & sourcing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre compras e contratação na obra — procurement, cotação, fornecedores e seleção — para conversar com o cliente sobre sourcing.
lessons.overview:
Procurement means buying. Sourcing means finding the right supplier. On a big project, this is a key job. We need steel, concrete, glass, and many systems. We must buy them at the right price and at the right time. Good procurement protects the cost and the schedule.

At Racional, the team sends an RFQ to many suppliers. The RFQ asks for a price. Each supplier sends a quote. We compare the quotes. We do not always pick the lowest price. We pick the best value. For a Microsoft or Amazon data center, quality and lead time are very important.

As a contract manager, you talk about procurement with the client. You explain the shortlist, the scope of supply, and the cost saving. When the choice is clear, we award the contract and send a purchase order. This lesson gives you the words to do that in English.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases simples de compras: "We send an RFQ to three suppliers.", "We compare the quotes." e "We award the contract to the best value."

Pratique descrever os passos: pedir cotação, comparar, escolher e emitir o pedido de compra (purchase order).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de status, o cliente americano quer saber como a Racional escolhe os fornecedores. Você explica o processo de procurement em inglês simples.
lessons.context: Our procurement process is clear. First, we send an RFQ to three suppliers. Each supplier sends a quote. We compare the quotes. We do not always pick the lowest price. We pick the best value. Then we award the contract and send a purchase order. We watch the lead time, because it protects the schedule.

lessons.title: Imports, lead times & containers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre importação de materiais — prazos de entrega, containers e atrasos de logística — para alinhar expectativas de prazo com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Some materials come from other countries. We import them. They travel by sea, inside a container. The ship goes to a port. Then the material must clear customs. All of this takes time. The total time is the lead time.

At Racional, imports are common on big projects. A data center for Amazon or Google may need special equipment from abroad. We place an order early. We work with a freight forwarder. We watch the supply chain every week. A long lead time can be a real risk for the schedule.

As a contract manager, you must explain this to the client. You talk about shipping, customs clearance, and possible delay. You add a buffer to protect the schedule. This lesson gives you the words to align dates with the client in English.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases simples de importação: "We import this material by sea.", "The lead time is ten weeks." e "We add a buffer to protect the schedule."

Pratique falar de prazos, containers e do risco de atraso na alfândega (customs).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano quer saber por que um equipamento demora a chegar. Você explica a importação e o prazo em inglês simples.
lessons.context: This equipment comes from abroad. We import it by sea, in a container. The ship goes to the port of Santos. Then the material must clear customs. The total lead time is ten weeks. So we place the order early. We add a buffer. This protects the schedule.

vocab.example: The lead time is ten weeks.

lessons.title: Personal hobbies & sports (cycling, swimming, walking)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, sobre seus hobbies e esportes favoritos — pedalar, nadar, caminhar — usando isso para criar vínculo com o cliente fora da reunião formal.
lessons.overview:
Work is not the only topic with a client. People also talk about life. They talk about hobbies and sports. This is called small talk. It builds a real connection. A good relationship makes the whole project easier.

Many people enjoy simple sports. They like cycling, swimming, or just to go for a walk. They do it on the weekend, outdoors, in the fresh air. It helps them relax and stay in shape. These are easy and friendly topics.

At Racional, a project with Microsoft or Amazon can last 18 to 24 months. That is a long time. You meet the same people again and again. Small talk about a hobby helps you build trust. This lesson gives you simple words to connect with the client like a person, not only like a manager.
lessons.intro:

Pratique falar do que você gosta de fazer no tempo livre, com tom amigável e descontraído.

lessons.title: Supplier qualification
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, a qualificação de um fornecedor — pedindo certificações, capacidade e histórico — para mostrar ao cliente americano que a Racional só contrata quem cumpre o padrão.
lessons.overview:
Before we hire a supplier, we check them. This is called supplier qualification. We do not hire a vendor only for a low price. We must be sure they are reliable. We must be sure they can do the job well and on time.

We look at three things. First, the certifications. Second, the production capacity. Third, the track record — their past work and good references. We also check the lead time. If a vendor is compliant and strong, we put them on the shortlist.

At Racional, this matters a lot. For a Microsoft or Amazon data center, quality cannot fail. The client wants proof that we hire only good vendors. As a contract manager, you ask the right questions to qualify a supplier. This lesson gives you the words to do that in English.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases simples para qualificar um fornecedor: "Do you have the right certifications?", "What is your production capacity?" e "Can you meet our lead time?"

Pratique pedir certificações, capacidade e histórico (track record) com perguntas curtas e diretas.
lessons.situation: Você avalia um novo fornecedor antes de colocá-lo na shortlist de um data center. O cliente americano acompanha a reunião. Você conduz a qualificação em inglês simples.
lessons.context: Before we hire you, we need to qualify you as a supplier. First, do you have the right certifications? Second, what is your production capacity? Can you scale up if we need more? Third, what is your track record? Please send two references. We need a reliable vendor who can meet our requirements and our lead time.

lessons.title: Supplier performance reviews
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, uma reunião de avaliação de desempenho de fornecedor — dizendo o que foi bem, o que precisa melhorar e qual a próxima ação — para manter a obra dentro do prazo e do custo.
lessons.overview:
After a supplier works for us, we check their work. This is a performance review. We look at the facts. Did they deliver on time? Did they meet expectations? Was the quality good? A good review is fair and clear.

We use simple words. The vendor can be on track, above expectations, or below target. We look at KPIs, like on-time delivery. We give clear feedback. We say what went well and the area to improve. If a vendor underperforms, we make a recovery plan.

At Racional, this keeps the project on time and on cost. For a Microsoft or Amazon data center, every vendor must be consistent. As a contract manager, you lead this review with respect and clear data. This lesson gives you the words to do that in English.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases simples de avaliação: "Your on-time delivery is good.", "Quality is below target." e "The next step is a recovery plan."

Pratique a estrutura: o que foi bem (what went well), o que melhorar (area to improve) e a próxima ação (next step).
lessons.situation: Você conduz a reunião trimestral de desempenho de um fornecedor. O cliente americano quer ver os dados. Você dá o feedback em inglês simples.
lessons.context: Let's start the performance review. First, what went well. Your on-time delivery is good. You are on track. Now, the area to improve. The quality is below target. This is our main KPI. So, the next step is a recovery plan. We need consistent work. Can you deliver on time and meet our expectations?

lessons.title: Subcontractor management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai coordenar subcontratados na obra em inglês simples — alinhando escopo, sequência e a passagem de frente entre as equipes.
lessons.overview:
On a big project, many companies work at the same time. The structure team, the MEP team (electrical, plumbing, HVAC), the facade team and the finishes team are all on site. Each company is a subcontractor. Each one does one trade. Your job is to make them work together.

The hard part is not inside one trade. The hard part is the interface — the point where one team stops and the next team starts. This is the handover. If the first team does not clear the area, the next team waits. And waiting means delay.

At Racional, this is the daily work of the contract manager. A data center for Microsoft or Amazon has hundreds of workers. You plan the sequence of trades. You coordinate the handovers. Good coordination keeps the schedule on track. This is how you control time and cost on a large build.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar três frases-âncora para a reunião de coordenação: "The MEP crew has to clear the area first." (a equipe de MEP precisa liberar a área primeiro), "This is outside your scope of work." (isto está fora do seu escopo) e "The handover is on Friday." (a passagem de frente é na sexta).

Use frases curtas. Uma ideia por frase. O foco é deixar a sequência clara para cada subcontratado.
lessons.situation: Reunião de coordenação na obra de um data center. O subcontratado de drywall não pode começar porque o de MEP ainda não liberou a área. Você precisa acertar a sequência com o cliente norte-americano presente.
lessons.context: We have many trades on site this week. The MEP crew needs to finish the rough-in. Then they clear the area. After that, the drywall team can start. The handover is on Friday. This sequence is important for the schedule.

lessons.title: Quality control & specifications
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar sobre controle de qualidade em inglês simples — dizer se um serviço atende à especificação e o que fazer quando está fora do padrão.
lessons.overview:
Every part of a building has a specification, or spec. The spec says how the work must be done. Concrete strength, paint color, pipe size — all of this is in the spec. Quality control (QC) checks if the work follows the spec.

When the work follows the spec, we say it meets the spec. When it does not, it is out of spec. Then we open a non-conformity report (NCR). The team must redo the work. A small defect early can cost a lot later.

At Racional, the North American client cares a lot about quality. A hospital or a data center must be safe and exact. The contract manager talks about QC every day. You check the finish, you control the tolerance, and you say clearly when something must be fixed. Clear words protect the schedule and the relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar frases-âncora de qualidade: "This meets the spec." (isto atende à especificação), "This is out of spec." (isto está fora do padrão) e "The team has to redo it." (a equipe precisa refazer).

Lembre que "to comply with" significa "estar em conformidade com". Frases curtas e diretas: você precisa ser claro sobre aprovar ou rejeitar.
lessons.situation: Inspeção de acabamento com o cliente norte-americano. Uma parede está fora da tolerância de prumo. Você precisa dizer que está fora da especificação e pedir o retrabalho.
lessons.context: Let's check the wall. The spec says the tolerance is three millimeters. This wall is out of tolerance. So it is out of spec. We will open an NCR. The team has to redo this part.

lessons.title: Holidays & traditions (Thanksgiving, July 4th)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conversar sobre feriados e tradições dos Estados Unidos em inglês simples — criando conexão com o cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
The United States has two big holidays that people love. The first is Thanksgiving, in November. Families gather at home. They eat turkey. They say what they are grateful for. It is a warm family day.

The second is the Fourth of July, also called Independence Day. There are fireworks at night. People have a cookout or a barbecue. It is summer, so it is a fun long weekend. Many people travel.

Why does this matter for Racional? Your client is North American. A small question about the holiday builds trust. "How was your Thanksgiving?" is an easy and kind question. When you know the tradition, you connect as people, not only as a contractor. This soft talk makes the hard talk easier.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar frases de conexão: "How was your Thanksgiving?" (como foi seu Dia de Ação de Graças?), "Did you enjoy the long weekend?" (você aproveitou o feriado prolongado?) e "Happy Fourth of July!" (feliz 4 de julho!).

O tom aqui é leve e pessoal. Frases curtas, perguntas simples. O objetivo é criar conexão, não falar de obra.

lessons.title: Quality assurance & inspections
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conduzir uma inspeção de qualidade em inglês simples — agendar, percorrer a obra, aprovar ou apontar um problema.
lessons.overview:
Quality assurance (QA) is the system that makes quality happen. Inspection is the action: you go and check the work. Before some steps, there is a hold point. The team cannot continue until the inspector says yes.

To do an inspection, you walk the site with the inspector. You check the work as per the drawings. If it is good, you sign off and the team can proceed. If you see a problem, you flag the issue. Sometimes a third-party inspector comes and issues a report.

At Racional, this is key before a concrete pour. You check the rebar first. The North American client often asks for QA records on hospitals and data centers. When the work is compliant, you sign off with confidence. Clear inspection talk keeps the build moving and safe.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar frases-âncora de inspeção: "Let's schedule the inspection." (vamos agendar a inspeção), "This is a hold point." (este é um ponto de parada) e "It is compliant. I sign off." (está conforme. Eu libero).

Lembre que "as per the drawings" significa "conforme os desenhos / projeto". Use frases curtas para aprovar ("sign off") ou apontar ("flag an issue").
lessons.situation: Inspeção antes da concretagem de uma laje, com inspetor terceirizado e o cliente norte-americano. Você precisa verificar a armadura e liberar (ou não) a concretagem.
lessons.context: Today we have a hold point. We cannot pour the concrete yet. First, we walk the site. We check the rebar as per the drawings. If it is compliant, I sign off. Then the team can proceed with the pour.

lessons.title: Schedule management & critical path
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar sobre cronograma e caminho crítico em inglês simples — dizer se a obra está no prazo, adiantada ou atrasada.
lessons.overview:
The schedule is the plan of time for the project. It shows the sequence of activities and the milestones. Some activities are on the critical path. These are the most important. If one of them is late, the whole project is late.

You always need to know your status. Are you on schedule, ahead of schedule, or behind schedule? Some tasks have float — extra time. Others have a hard deadline. When a task on the critical path starts to slip, this is your top priority.

At Racional, the contract manager tracks progress every week. A data center for Amazon or Google has a fixed delivery date. You watch the critical path. You watch the lead time of key materials. When you report "we are on schedule" to the client, you give them confidence. Clear schedule talk protects the contract.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar frases-âncora de prazo: "We are on schedule." (estamos no prazo), "This task is on the critical path." (esta tarefa está no caminho crítico) e "This is our top priority." (esta é a nossa prioridade máxima).

Lembre dos três status básicos: "on schedule" (no prazo), "ahead of schedule" (adiantado) e "behind schedule" (atrasado). Use frases curtas no presente simples.
lessons.situation: Reunião semanal de status com o cliente norte-americano. Uma entrega de material está com prazo apertado e pode afetar o caminho crítico. Você precisa reportar a situação.
lessons.context: Let me give you the status. Most of the work is on schedule. But one task is on the critical path. The lead time for this material is long. If it slips, the project slips. So this is our top priority this week.

lessons.title: Schedule recovery plans
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai apresentar um plano de recuperação de prazo em inglês simples — explicar o atraso, a causa e as ações para voltar ao cronograma.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a project falls behind. There is a delay. Then you need a recovery plan. This is a clear plan to recover time and get back on track. A good manager does not hide the problem. A good manager brings a plan.

First, you find the root cause — the real reason for the delay. Then you choose actions. You can add a crew. You can run an extra shift. You can fast-track some activities. Each action has a cost, so you choose with care to mitigate the delay.

At Racional, the North American client respects honesty. "To be honest with you, we are two weeks behind" is a strong, professional thing to say. Then you show the action plan and the new recovery date. You explain how the team will catch up. A clear recovery plan protects trust and protects the contract.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar frases-âncora do plano de recuperação: "To be honest with you, we are behind." (sendo honesto, estamos atrasados), "We have a recovery plan." (temos um plano de recuperação) e "We will add a crew to catch up." (vamos adicionar uma equipe para recuperar).

A estrutura é: assumir o atraso, dar a causa-raiz, apresentar o plano e a nova data. Frases curtas e honestas.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o cliente norte-americano para reportar um atraso de duas semanas no data center. Você precisa assumir o problema e apresentar o plano de recuperação com uma nova data.
lessons.context: To be honest with you, we are two weeks behind. The root cause was the late delivery of steel. But we have a recovery plan. We will add a crew and run an extra shift. The new recovery date is June fifteenth.

lessons.title: Cost control & budget tracking
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você dará um status de custo claro ao cliente americano — comparando o gasto real com o orçamento, explicando o desvio e falando de fatura e pagamento.
lessons.overview:
Cost control means you watch the money on the project. There is a budget. This is the money you plan to spend. There is an actual cost. This is the money you really spend. The difference is the variance. At Racional, this is part of the daily job on every site, from offices to hospitals and data centers.

The client wants a clear picture every month. North American clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google watch the numbers closely. They want to know one thing fast: are we over budget or under budget? A good contract manager always shows the number and compares it to the plan. A number alone is not enough.

Good cost control builds trust. When you track every cost against the budget, the client feels safe. You can explain the cash flow, the invoice, and the payment with confidence. This is how Racional shows control on big, long projects.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai usar três frases-âncora: "The actual cost is under budget.", "We have a small variance on steel." e "We track the cost against the budget every month."

Lembre-se da regra de ouro: nunca dê só um número — sempre compare o real com o orçado (actual versus budget).
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de custo com o controller do cliente americano. Ele quer saber como o gasto real está em relação ao orçamento e se há algum desvio.
lessons.context: Let me show you the numbers. The actual cost is under budget this month. We have a small variance on steel, but the contingency covers it. Our cash flow is good. We sent the invoice last week, and the payment is on time.

vocab.example: The budget for this phase is approved.

We are within the approved amount.

lessons.title: Music talk 4: Jamiroquai — acid jazz & dance
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversará sobre música com o cliente — falando de Jamiroquai, ritmo e dança — para criar uma conexão leve e humana fora da pauta da obra.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. Before a meeting starts, a short talk about music is warm and easy. Jamiroquai is a British band. They play acid jazz and funky music. The songs have a strong groove and a happy beat. This kind of feel-good music is perfect for small talk.

For a contract manager at Racional, these small moments matter. A project with a North American client can last 18 to 24 months. You meet the same people many times. A light talk about a band or a song builds a real bond, meeting after meeting.

You do not need to be an expert. You can say what you like and ask what they like. "This song is upbeat. It makes me tap my foot." Or: "I am more of a listener, not a dancer." Simple words are enough to start a friendly conversation.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE: o foco é conexão, não a obra. Você vai usar frases leves como "I like this band.", "This song is really upbeat." e "I'm more of a listener."

O tom é de bate-papo: pergunte o que o cliente gosta e diga o que você gosta. Música é uma porta fácil para criar rapport.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, você e o cliente americano esperam o café. Ele comenta que gosta de música e a conversa flui para Jamiroquai e ritmos para dançar.
