lessons.title: Forecasting cost-at-completion
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fará uma projeção de custo final ao cliente — falando do gasto até agora, do que falta gastar e da estimativa de fechamento dentro do orçamento.
lessons.overview:
A forecast is a look into the future. In a project, you must answer one big question: how much will the project cost at the end? This number is the cost-at-completion. It is not the cost today. It is the final cost when all the work is done.

The math is simple. You take the cost to date, the money you already spent. Then you add the cost to complete, the money for the remaining work. Together they give you the cost-at-completion. At Racional, this number tells the client if the project will land within budget.

North American clients value an honest forecast. If you see a problem early, you give an early warning. This is good, not bad. A clear projection shows you watch the trend and you control the job. On a hyperscale data center, this trust is worth a lot.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula CORE você junta duas partes para olhar o futuro: "cost to date" (o que já gastamos) + "cost to complete" (o que falta gastar) = "cost-at-completion" (custo final).

Frase-âncora: "We forecast to land within budget." Use "early warning" quando vir um problema chegando.
lessons.situation: Reunião de revisão de custo. O cliente americano quer saber sua melhor estimativa do custo final do projeto e se vai fechar dentro do orçamento.
lessons.context: Here is my forecast. The cost to date is on plan. The remaining work has a clear cost to complete. My best estimate is that we land within budget. The trend is good. I see no risk today.

lessons.title: HSE 1: safety culture on-site
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará de cultura de segurança na obra em inglês — falando de EPI, perigos, quase-acidentes e da regra de parar o trabalho quando algo está inseguro.
lessons.overview:
Safety is the number one priority on every site. Safety culture means that every person, from the worker to the manager, thinks about safety first. At Racional, on offices, hospitals, and data centers, no schedule and no cost is more important than the safety of the team.

The basics are clear. Every person must wear the right PPE: a hard hat, boots, and a vest. The team looks for any hazard, a thing that can hurt someone. Before the work starts, a short toolbox talk reminds the team of the risks of the day.

North American clients like Microsoft and Amazon watch safety very closely. They like the idea of stop-work authority. This means any person can stop the work when something is not safe. A near miss is also important: it is a close call, an accident that almost happened. We always report it to learn and to prevent the next one.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula CORE abre o eixo de HSE (segurança). As frases-âncora são: "Everyone must wear PPE.", "Safety is our number one priority." e "Anyone can stop the work if it is not safe."

Termos centrais: hazard (perigo), near miss (quase-acidente) e to report (reportar). Segurança é o tema que mais impressiona o cliente americano.
lessons.situation: Visita do cliente americano à obra. Ele quer entender sua cultura de segurança e como o time lida com riscos e quase-acidentes no dia a dia.
lessons.context: Safety is our number one priority. Everyone must wear PPE: a hard hat, boots, and a vest. We start each day with a toolbox talk. If we see a hazard, we report it. Anyone can stop the work when it is not safe.

lessons.title: HSE 2: international safety programs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará de programas internacionais de segurança em inglês — citando padrões como OSHA, auditorias, indicadores como TRIR e ações corretivas.
lessons.overview:
Big international clients have strong safety standards. In the United States, the main one is OSHA. When a project follows the rules, we say it is compliant. Compliance means we do what the standard asks. At Racional, this is key to work for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google.

Clients check safety with numbers and with visits. A safety audit or an inspection looks at the site. They watch indicators like TRIR and the number of lost-time injuries. A good safety record opens doors. The goal of many programs is zero harm: nobody gets hurt.

When an audit finds a problem, the team takes a corrective action. The safety officer tracks each action to the end. This shows the client that Racional does not just meet the standard on paper. We live it on the site, every day, on every project.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula CORE continua o eixo de HSE, agora com o vocabulário dos programas internacionais. Frases-âncora: "We are OSHA compliant.", "We track the TRIR every month." e "Our goal is zero harm."

Termos-chave: compliant (em conformidade), safety audit (auditoria) e corrective action (ação corretiva).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pergunta como sua obra se alinha aos padrões internacionais de segurança e como você acompanha os indicadores e auditorias.
lessons.context: We follow international safety standards. We are OSHA compliant. We track the TRIR every month. After each safety audit, we take a corrective action. Our goal is zero harm. We have a strong safety record.

lessons.title: HSE 3: incident reporting & investigation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reportará uma ocorrência ao cliente em inglês — descrevendo o que aconteceu, a causa-raiz, a ação corretiva e as lições aprendidas.
lessons.overview:
When something goes wrong on a site, the team must report it. An incident is an event that causes harm or damage. A near miss is a close call, with no harm this time. Even a small one matters. At Racional, we write an incident report for every event, big or small.

After the report, we look for the root cause. This is the real reason behind the event. Maybe a worker slipped, or someone dropped a tool. The investigation asks "why?" until it finds the true cause, not just the surface.

The last step is the most important. We take a corrective action to fix the cause. We write the lessons learned and share them. This is how we prevent the next event. North American clients trust a team that reports openly and learns fast, on every project, from hospitals to data centers.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula CORE fecha o eixo de HSE com o relato de ocorrências. Frases-âncora: "We had a near miss today.", "We found the root cause." e "We took a corrective action to prevent it."

Termos-chave: incident report (relatório), root cause (causa-raiz) e lessons learned (lições aprendidas).
lessons.situation: Houve um quase-acidente na obra. Você precisa reportar ao cliente americano o que aconteceu, a causa-raiz e a ação tomada.
lessons.context: We had a near miss today. A worker dropped a tool, but nobody was hurt. We stopped the work. We wrote an incident report and found the root cause. We took a corrective action to prevent it next time.

lessons.title: American cities & business hubs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você puxa uma conversa leve com o cliente norte-americano sobre cidades e polos de negócios dos Estados Unidos, criando conexão antes da reunião.
lessons.overview:
The United States has many big cities. Each city has a business hub and its own feeling. New York is famous for finance. Chicago is famous for tall skyscrapers. Houston and Dallas work with energy and construction. Seattle and San Francisco are famous for technology. Your North American clients often come from these places.

This matters for your work. Racional builds data centers for Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. The people from these companies live and work in American cities. When you talk about their city, you show interest. A small talk about a city can start a good relationship.

You do not need long sentences. You can say "Where are you based?" or "Have you ever been to São Paulo?" You can ask about the weather, the traffic, or the commute. These simple questions make the client feel welcome before the meeting starts.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE — mais leve, de relacionamento. O objetivo não é técnica de obra, é conexão com o cliente americano.

Guarde duas frases-âncora simples: "Where are you based?" (Onde você fica baseado?) e "Have you ever been to São Paulo?" (Você já esteve em São Paulo?). Pergunte sobre a cidade do cliente antes de falar da sua.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião começar, o cliente americano comenta que voou de Chicago. Você puxa uma conversa leve sobre a cidade e os polos de negócios dos EUA.
lessons.context: So you flew in from Chicago? I love that city. The skyscrapers are amazing. Where are you based, downtown or in the suburbs? I have never been to Chicago, but I'd love to visit one day.

vocab.example: New York is a big business hub.
New York is on the East Coast.
Seattle is on the West Coast.
I flew in from Dallas today.
Have you ever been to Brazil?

exercises.explanation: 'Where are you based?' é a forma profissional e calorosa de perguntar onde a pessoa fica baseada.

exercises.title: 3. Fale com o cliente antes da reunião

exercises.explanation: Curiosidade genuína pela cidade do outro é o jeito mais simples de transformar uma conversa em vínculo.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, comente sobre uma cidade dos EUA que você gostaria de visitar e diga por quê. Depois pergunte ao cliente sobre a cidade onde ele mora. Pode misturar inglês e português.

lessons.title: Tropicalização 3: labor regulations & desvio de função
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao cliente norte-americano, em inglês simples, como a lei trabalhista brasileira molda decisões na obra, incluindo jornada, horas extras e o desvio de função.
lessons.overview:
Brazil has strong labor laws. These laws protect the worker. They set the working hours, the rules for overtime, and the rights of each person on site. A North American client thinks with American rules. So you need to explain why our rules are different.

One idea is hard to translate: desvio de função. In Brazil, a worker must do the job they were hired for. If a worker does a very different role, the company can face a labor claim. This is a real risk, and it can cost time and money on a Racional project.

This matters every day for a contract manager. The client may ask one person to do two jobs. You must explain, with calm words, that we always comply with the law. Good compliance protects the project and the client. You do not just say "no". You explain the reason and you offer a safer way.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do eixo de tropicalização — adaptar práticas internacionais à realidade brasileira.

Guarde a frase-âncora: "A worker must do the job they were hired for." (Um trabalhador deve fazer a função para a qual foi contratado.) E nunca diga só "that's the law here": explique o porquê e o risco.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano quer que um eletricista também opere uma máquina. Você explica, com tato, por que a lei trabalhista brasileira exige cuidado com o desvio de função.
lessons.context: In Brazil, labor law is strict. A worker must do the job they were hired for. If we ask the electrician to run that machine, that is a different role. It can create a labor claim. Let me show you a safer way.

vocab.example: The working hours are fixed by law.
The night shift has special rules.
He was hired for one role.
This can lead to a labor claim.
We would face a legal risk.
Let me clarify how it works.

exercises.explanation: Esta é a frase central para explicar o desvio de função em inglês simples.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a explicação
exercises.explanation: 'A different role can create a labor claim' explica o risco do desvio de função de forma clara.

exercises.title: 3. Estar em conformidade
exercises.prompt: We always ___ ___ the labor law to protect the project.
exercises.explanation: 'To comply with' = cumprir, estar de acordo com. É o verbo certo para falar de leis e normas.

exercises.title: 4. Explique o desvio de função
exercises.prompt: O cliente quer que um eletricista opere outra máquina. Qual frase explica melhor o risco?

options.text: No problem, anyone can do any job here.
options.whyWrong: Isso é falso e perigoso, pode gerar passivo trabalhista.

options.text: That is a different role, so it can create a labor claim.
We do not follow any labor law on site.
options.whyWrong: Soa irresponsável e não é verdade, a Racional cumpre a lei.

exercises.explanation: Explicar que é 'a different role' e pode gerar 'a labor claim' mostra domínio do tema e protege o projeto.

exercises.title: 5. Explique ao cliente
exercises.targetText: In Brazil, labor law is strict, and we comply with it. A worker must do the job they were hired for. Let me show you a safer way.
exercises.translation: No Brasil, a lei trabalhista é rígida, e nós a cumprimos. Um trabalhador deve fazer a função para a qual foi contratado. Deixa eu te mostrar uma forma mais segura.
exercises.prompt: O cliente quer mudar a função de um trabalhador. Explique a regra com tato, em voz alta.
exercises.explanation: Firme no conteúdo, gentil no tom, e sempre com uma solução. É assim que se tropicaliza uma decisão sem criar atrito.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, explique a um cliente americano uma diferença entre a lei trabalhista do Brasil e a dos EUA que afeta a sua obra, e qual risco ela traz. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can say that Brazilian labor law is strict.
I can explain that a worker must do the job they were hired for.
I can warn that a different role can create a labor claim.
I can say that we comply with the labor law.
I can explain a rule and offer a safer option.

lessons.title: Commissioning & handover
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, as etapas de comissionamento e entrega da obra ao cliente norte-americano: testes, pendências, aceite e documentação final.
lessons.overview:
The last phase of a project is very important. First comes commissioning. This means we test every system: power, water, and air. We prove that each system works well. This phase is critical in data centers and hospitals, where systems cannot fail.

When a system is not ready, it becomes a pending item. We write all pending items on the punch list. Some items are small. Some items are blockers and stop the delivery. The team closes the punch list before the handover.

Then comes the handover. We give the project to the client. We deliver the as-built drawings, the manuals, and the certificates. The client gives a sign-off to approve the work. For a Racional contract manager, "ready" means tested, documented, and signed. The warranty starts after this moment.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre a fase final da obra: commissioning (comissionamento) e handover (entrega).

Guarde a frase-âncora: "All systems are commissioned. We are ready for handover." (Todos os sistemas estão comissionados. Estamos prontos para a entrega.) Nunca diga "está pronto" antes de fechar a punch list.
lessons.situation: Reunião de entrega de um data center. O cliente americano quer saber se os sistemas estão comissionados e se a obra está pronta para o aceite final.
lessons.context: All major systems are commissioned and tested. We closed the punch list last week. Only two small items remain, and they are not blockers. We are ready for handover. The as-built drawings are ready for your sign-off.

vocab.example: The punch list has two items left.
One pending item is the door lock.

exercises.explanation: Status claro, pendências nomeadas, próximo passo definido. É o relatório de entrega que o cliente americano espera.

exercises.title: 3. O que é a punch list?

exercises.explanation: 'Punch list' é a lista de pendências a corrigir antes do aceite. Fechá-la é o que libera o handover.

exercises.targetText: All major systems are commissioned and tested. We are ready for handover, and the as-built drawings are ready for your sign-off.

exercises.prompt: Na reunião de entrega do data center, informe o status em voz alta.

lessons.title: Sustainability & green building (LEED)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre sustentabilidade e construção verde, incluindo a certificação LEED, para acompanhar as exigências ambientais do cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
North American clients care a lot about sustainability. The big technology companies with data centers want high green standards. They ask for a green building that uses less energy and less water. For Racional, this is part of every modern project.

The main green label is LEED. It is an American certification with levels: Certified, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. A project earns points for green choices. We can use energy-efficient systems, recycled materials, and renewable energy. We can reuse water and cut waste on site.

This matters in daily talks with the client. Each green choice has a real benefit: more LEED points, less energy use, and a lower carbon footprint. When you connect a green choice to a benefit, the client sees value. Sustainability is also performance and cost.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre sustainability (sustentabilidade) e green building (construção verde).

Guarde a frase-âncora: "This project is targeting LEED Gold. We reduce energy use and we reuse water." Ligue sempre cada escolha verde a um benefício concreto.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano de um data center quer saber como a obra contribui para a certificação LEED. Você explica as escolhas sustentáveis do projeto.
lessons.context: This project is targeting LEED Gold. We reduce energy use with efficient cooling. We reuse rainwater on site, and most of our steel is recycled. These choices earn LEED points and lower the carbon footprint.

lessons.title: BIM & construction tech
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre BIM e tecnologia de construção (modelos 3D, detecção de conflitos e dados da obra) para acompanhar a inovação que o cliente norte-americano valoriza.
lessons.overview:
Modern construction uses a lot of technology. The most important tool is BIM, or Building Information Modeling. It is a smart 3D model of the building. It puts all the systems together: structure, electrical, water, and air. North American clients, especially in data centers, expect this digital way of working.

One great feature is clash detection. The software finds a clash where, for example, a duct hits a beam. It finds the problem in the model, before construction. So the team avoids rework on site. Less rework means less cost and less delay for a Racional project.

There are more tools too. We use drones for weekly photos and laser scanning to measure the site. A dashboard shows real-time data about cost and schedule. With this we track progress every day. The key message for the client is always the benefit: more accuracy, less rework, more control.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre BIM e construction tech (tecnologia de construção).

Guarde a frase-âncora: "We use a 3D BIM model. Clash detection saves time and money on site." Não fale de tecnologia pela tecnologia: diga sempre o benefício.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano quer saber como a obra usa tecnologia para reduzir erros. Você explica como o BIM e a detecção de conflitos ajudam o projeto.
lessons.context: We use a full 3D BIM model. It puts structure, power, and air in one model. Clash detection finds conflicts before construction, so we avoid rework on site. We also use a drone for weekly photos. This saves time and money.

lessons.title: Being hosted in the US
lessons.objective: Nesta aula-ponte (BRIDGE) você aprende a se comportar com naturalidade e cortesia quando for recebido por um cliente nos Estados Unidos: agradecer, conversar à mesa e retribuir a hospitalidade.
lessons.overview:
During a long project, the client may invite you to the US. You may visit the head office, go to dinner, or be a guest at his home. American culture values courtesy and a warm "thank you". When the client is your host, simple words make a big difference.

At the table, it is natural to praise the food and the place. You can say "This is delicious" or "Thank you for having me". You can thank the hospitality with a simple sentence: "It's very kind of you." If the client pays the bill, just say thank you. These small words show respect.

It is also good to return the favor. You can say "Next time you're in Brazil, dinner is on me" and "I'd love to show you around São Paulo". For a Racional contract manager, a project can last 18 to 24 months. These warm moments build a long and strong relationship with the client.

lessons.title: Meeting fundamentals: agenda, minutes, action items
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz o esqueleto de uma reunião de obra em inglês — abre com a pauta, registra os pontos e atribui as tarefas com prazo.
lessons.overview:
Every meeting needs a plan. The plan is the agenda. The agenda is the list of items. It shows what you will talk about. A good agenda keeps the meeting short. It keeps the team on track. As a contract manager, you run many meetings on site. You need a clear agenda for each one.

During the meeting, someone writes the minutes. The minutes are the notes. They show what the team decided. They also show the action items. An action item is a task. Every action item has an owner and a deadline. The owner is the person who does the task. The deadline is the day it is due.

At Racional, you work with big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These clients want clear minutes after every meeting. They want to know who does what, and when. Good meeting notes build trust. They show that the team is in control of the project. This is a key skill on every site.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você aprende a estrutura básica de uma reunião em inglês. Três frases-âncora vão guiar você: "Let's start with the agenda" (vamos começar pela pauta), "The action item is..." (a tarefa é...) e "The deadline is..." (o prazo é...).

Note a diferença simples: agenda é o plano (antes), minutes são as notas (durante e depois). Cada tarefa precisa de um owner (responsável) e uma deadline (prazo).
lessons.situation: Você abre a reunião semanal de obra com um cliente norte-americano. Precisa apresentar a pauta, registrar as decisões e atribuir tarefas com prazo.
lessons.context: Good morning. Let's start with the agenda. We have three items today. First, the schedule. Second, the costs. Third, safety. I will take notes. Each task has an owner and a deadline. Let's begin.

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você se apresenta com segurança numa primeira reunião com o cliente — diz seu nome, seu cargo e o que você faz na obra.
lessons.overview:
The first meeting is important. It is the first time you meet the client. People shake hands and say their names. They say their role on the project. A good start builds trust. As a contract manager, you are the main point of contact on site. The client must know your name and your role from day one.

To introduce yourself is simple. You say your first name. You say your job. You say what you are responsible for. You can also ask about the other person. This is how you connect. A warm first meeting makes the next months easier.

At Racional, your counterpart is often North American. The client comes from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google. They visit the data center or the office project. They want to know the team. A clear and friendly introduction shows that Racional is professional. It opens the door to a good relationship.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você monta sua apresentação pessoal em inglês. Três frases-âncora: "Nice to meet you" (prazer em conhecer), "I'm the contract manager" (sou o gerente de contrato) e "I'm responsible for the site" (sou responsável pela obra).

Lembre: role é o seu papel/cargo, point of contact é a pessoa que o cliente procura, e counterpart é a pessoa equivalente a você do lado do cliente.

lessons.title: Conference calls & virtual meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa de uma conference call em inglês — pede para repetir, confirma o que entendeu e cuida da conexão e do áudio.
lessons.overview:
Many meetings happen online today. This is a conference call or a virtual meeting. People join from many places. Sometimes the sound is bad. Sometimes you cannot hear. You need simple words to fix this. You can say "Can you hear me?" or "Could you repeat that?" These short phrases save the meeting.

On a call, you also need to manage your audio. You mute when you do not speak. You unmute to talk. You can share your screen to show a plan. Sometimes a person drops off and joins again. This is normal. Stay calm and confirm what you hear.

At Racional, you have many calls with clients in the United States. The client may be at a Microsoft or Amazon office far away. A clear call keeps the project on track. When you ask people to speak slower or to confirm, you avoid mistakes. Good call skills protect the schedule and the budget.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você ganha as frases de sobrevivência da call em inglês. Âncoras: "Can you hear me?" (você me ouve?), "Could you repeat that?" (pode repetir?) e "Let me confirm" (deixa eu confirmar).

Lembre: to mute é silenciar o microfone, to unmute é reativar, e to drop off é cair da chamada. São verbos curtos e muito usados.
lessons.situation: Você está numa conference call com o cliente nos EUA. O áudio falha em alguns momentos e você precisa pedir para repetir e confirmar os pontos.
lessons.context: Hello, can you hear me? Sorry, you are breaking up. Could you repeat that, please? Could you speak a little slower? Let me confirm: the deadline is Friday. I will share my screen now.

lessons.title: Status updates — weekly
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você dá o status semanal da obra em inglês — diz o que está no prazo, o que está atrasado e quais são os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
Every week you give a status update. The update is short. It tells the client where the project is. Some tasks are on track. Some tasks are behind schedule. A few may be ahead of schedule. The client wants the truth. A clear weekly update keeps everyone calm and informed.

In a status update, you talk about milestones and next steps. A milestone is a key point in the project. A next step is what the team will do soon. You also talk about a blocker — a problem that stops the work. When you flag a blocker early, the client can help fix it fast.

At Racional, the weekly update is part of the routine. On a data center for Amazon or Microsoft, time is money. A delay of one week can cost a lot. So you report clearly: what is done, what is late, and what comes next. Good weekly updates protect the schedule and the relationship with the client.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você estrutura o status semanal em inglês. Âncoras: "We are on track" (estamos no prazo), "This task is behind schedule" (esta tarefa está atrasada) e "The next step is..." (o próximo passo é...).

Lembre o par de opostos: on track (no prazo) x behind schedule (atrasado). E um blocker é o problema que trava a obra — você precisa flag (sinalizar) cedo.
lessons.situation: É a reunião semanal com o cliente norte-americano. Você precisa resumir o andamento da obra: o que avançou, o que atrasou e os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Here is the weekly update. Overall, we are on track. The foundation is complete. The steel work is in progress. One task is behind schedule because of the rain. I want to flag one blocker. The next step is the concrete.

vocab.example: We are on track this week.
The roof is ahead of schedule.
We will catch up next week.

I want to flag a risk.

exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos. O importante é contar o que avançou e o que ficou para trás.

lessons.title: Business trips to the US
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula-ponte você conversa de forma leve numa viagem de negócios aos Estados Unidos — fala da viagem, quebra o gelo e marca um café com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you travel to the United States for work. This is a business trip. You take a long flight. You may feel tired from the time change. This is jet lag. You arrive, you check in at the hotel, and you rest. The next day, you meet the client in person. Meeting in person builds a strong bond.

On a business trip, small talk is important. Small talk is light, friendly talk. You can talk about the flight, the weather, or sports. This helps you break the ice. American clients like a quick, warm chat before business. A simple question like "How was your flight?" opens the door.

At Racional, you work with North American clients all the time. A trip to a Microsoft or Amazon office is a big chance to connect. Good small talk makes the next meetings easier. People do business with people they like. So a friendly coffee and a few kind words matter as much as the numbers.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula-ponte (BRIDGE): o foco é conexão e cultura, não técnica. Âncoras leves: "How was your flight?" (como foi seu voo?), "Let's grab a coffee" (vamos tomar um café) e "This is my first time here" (é a minha primeira vez aqui).

Lembre: small talk é a conversa leve de aquecimento, e to break the ice é quebrar o gelo. Nos EUA, isso vem antes dos negócios.
lessons.situation: Você chega aos Estados Unidos para visitar o cliente. No primeiro encontro, faz uma conversa leve antes da reunião de trabalho.
lessons.context: Hi, nice to see you in person. How was your flight? Mine was long, so I have a little jet lag. This is my first time downtown. Let's grab a coffee before the meeting. Thank you for hosting us.

lessons.title: Status updates — monthly
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta o status mensal da obra em inglês — resume o progresso, o custo dentro do orçamento e a segurança do trabalho.
lessons.overview:
Once a month you give a bigger report. This is the monthly summary. It is longer than the weekly update. It shows the full picture of the project. You talk about the progress, the budget, and safety. The client wants to see the big numbers and the main risks. A clear monthly report shows that the project is under control.

In the monthly report, you use simple numbers. You say the project is percent complete. You say it is within budget or over budget. You talk about the scope and the headcount — the number of people on site. You also forecast the next month. This helps the client plan ahead.

At Racional, safety is always first. On a hospital or a data center for Microsoft or Amazon, one accident is one too many. So the monthly report shows safety numbers, like a lost-time incident. A strong safety record builds deep trust. It tells the client that Racional cares about people, not only deadlines.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você monta o resumo mensal em inglês. Âncoras: "We are 60 percent complete" (estamos 60% concluídos), "We are within budget" (estamos dentro do orçamento) e "Safety is good" (a segurança está em ordem).

Lembre o par within budget (dentro do orçamento) x over budget (acima do orçamento), e o termo de segurança lost-time incident (acidente com afastamento).
lessons.situation: É a reunião mensal com o cliente norte-americano. Você precisa resumir progresso, custo e segurança do trabalho do mês.
lessons.context: Here is the monthly summary. We are 60 percent complete. We are within budget. The cost is under control. Safety is good. We had zero accidents and zero lost-time incidents. I forecast a strong next month.

takeaways: I can give a monthly summary in English.

lessons.title: Status updates — quarterly business reviews
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a sua parte de uma revisão trimestral (QBR) com o cliente — abre a fala, mostra os resultados do trimestre, conecta com os objetivos do cliente e fecha olhando para a frente.
lessons.overview:
Every three months, a big project has a special meeting. We call it a quarterly review, or QBR. In this meeting, the contract manager shows the results of the last three months. He talks about the highlights and the main achievements. For a company like Racional, with data centers for Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, this meeting is very important.

The American client wants clear numbers. He wants to know one thing: are we on track? The contract manager shows what the team delivered. He shows that the project is on budget and safe. Good numbers build trust. Trust keeps the client calm and happy.

A QBR is not about small details from the site. It is about the big picture. The manager looks back at the quarter, and then he looks ahead to the next one. He shows that Racional is aligned with the client's go-live date. At the end, he always opens the floor for questions.
lessons.intro:
Pense numa fala curta em três partes. Abertura: "Thank you for your time. Today I will show our results." Corpo: "We delivered three milestones. We are on budget." Fechamento: "For next quarter, our focus is the final phase."

Use frases curtas e com números. Conecte sempre com o cliente: "We are aligned with your go-live date." E feche convidando perguntas: "I am happy to take questions."
lessons.situation: Revisão trimestral (QBR) com a diretoria do cliente norte-americano. Você conduz a sua fala: resultados do trimestre e a perspectiva para o próximo.
lessons.context: Good morning. Thank you for your time. Today I will show our results for the quarter. We delivered three key milestones. We are on budget and on track. We had zero accidents — a strong safety record. For next quarter, our focus is the final phase. We are aligned with your go-live date. Thank you. I am happy to take any questions.

lessons.title: Project kickoff meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa da reunião de início de projeto (kickoff) — apresenta a agenda, fala de escopo, prazo e papéis, e alinha as expectativas com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
A new project always starts with a special meeting. We call it the kickoff meeting. The team and the client meet for the first time. They look at the agenda together. They talk about the scope, the schedule, and the roles. Everyone needs to know one thing: who does what.

For Racional, a kickoff is the first step of a long journey. A data center or a hospital can take 18 to 24 months. So the team and the client must align from day one. They talk about the first milestones and the main deliverables. They also choose the point of contact for each side.

A good kickoff sets clear expectations. The contract manager walks through the plan, step by step. Then the team is ready to break ground and start the work on site. When the manager wraps up the meeting, everyone leaves with the same picture in mind.
lessons.intro:
A reunião de kickoff é a primeira com o cliente. Você precisa de frases simples para guiar a conversa. Agenda: "Let me walk through the agenda." Escopo: "The scope is the new data center."

No fim, alinhe expectativas e feche: "Let me wrap up. Our point of contact is Fernando."

lessons.title: Pre-construction meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma reunião de pré-obra (pre-construction) — fala de licenças, prazos de fornecimento, acesso ao canteiro e itens pendentes com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before the team starts to build, there is a key step: the pre-construction phase. In this phase, the contract manager checks many things. He checks the permits and the approvals. He plans how to mobilize the team to the site. Nothing can start without this work.

One big topic is time. Some materials have a long lead time. A long lead item can take many weeks to arrive. So Racional must procure these items early, often months in advance. For a data center, special equipment can come from another country. Good planning keeps the project on track.

The manager also plans the site access and the temporary facilities — offices, water, and power for the team. In the meeting with the American client, he confirms every detail. He shows the pending points and the next steps. A strong pre-construction meeting saves time and money later.
lessons.intro:
A reunião de pré-obra prepara tudo antes de começar. Você precisa falar de licenças e prazos. Licenças: "The permits are approved." Prazo de fornecimento: "This item has a long lead time."

Mostre o que está pendente e o que está no prazo: "We are on track. Two items are pending."

lessons.title: Long-term relationship building
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você mantém o relacionamento de longo prazo com o cliente — pergunta como a pessoa está, retoma o contato e cuida do vínculo durante todo o projeto.
lessons.overview:
A big project lasts a long time. A data center can take 18 to 24 months. In all this time, the contract manager talks to the same client again and again. So a good relationship is very important. The manager must stay in touch and build rapport with the American client.

This is not only about work. It is about people. The manager likes to check in and catch up. A simple question like "How have you been?" opens a warm talk. When you remember small things about a person, you show that you value the relationship. This builds trust.

Strong bonds help the whole partnership. They make hard talks easier later. A short coffee or a quick call keeps the connection alive. The manager always looks forward to the next meeting. Good relationships, built day by day, help Racional down the road, on this project and on the next one.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de relacionamento, com tom leve. O foco é a conexão humana, não a obra. Retomar contato: "It is great to catch up." Perguntar: "How have you been?"

Mostre que valoriza a pessoa: "Let's stay in touch." e "I look forward to our next chat."

lessons.title: Site meetings & toolbox talks
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma reunião de obra e um diálogo de segurança (toolbox talk) — fala de progresso, bloqueios, riscos e do uso de EPI com a equipe e o cliente.
lessons.overview:
On the site, the day often starts with a short meeting. We call it a site meeting or a toolbox talk. The team stands together for a few minutes. They talk about the work of the day and, most of all, about safety. For Racional, safety comes first on every project.

In this talk, the manager checks the progress and any blocker. But the main topic is risk. He points out every hazard. He reminds the team to wear a hard hat and full PPE. He tells everyone to watch out for trucks, holes, and open edges. Each shift begins with this safety check.

When something is not safe, anyone can flag it right away. A near miss is reported, even when no one is hurt. This keeps the project on schedule and the people safe. American clients value this. They want the team to stay alert all day, every day.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula é sobre a reunião de obra e o toolbox talk (diálogo de segurança). O foco é segurança. Risco: "Watch out for this hazard." EPI: "Please wear your hard hat."

Avise sobre o que parou e o que é perigoso: "Flag any blocker right away." e "Stay alert."

lessons.title: Brainstorming & ideation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa de uma sessão de brainstorming com a equipe e o cliente — propõe ideias, constrói sobre as ideias dos outros, pesa opções e ajuda a escolher uma solução.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a project hits a problem with no clear answer. Then the team meets to brainstorm. In a brainstorm, everyone shares ideas. There is no wrong idea at first. The goal is to come up with many options. Then the team can find the best way forward.

In this meeting, people throw out ideas with simple questions: "What if...?" or "How about...?". A good idea gets a warm reply: "Good point!". Then someone can build on it and make it better. The team stays open to every option, even a quick workaround.

After many ideas, the team must choose. They weigh the options and look at each trade-off. Some ideas are not feasible on a real site. In the end, the team settles on one plan. For Racional, this is how a contract manager and an American client solve hard problems together — fast and as a team.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula é sobre gerar e escolher ideias em grupo. Você precisa de frases para propor e para reagir. Propor: "What if we change the order?" e "How about a workaround?"

Reaja e escolha: "Good point. Let's build on that." e "Let's settle on this option."

lessons.context: We have a delay. Let's brainstorm. What if we change the order of the work? Good point. Let's build on that idea. How about a quick workaround for now? We need to weigh the options. This plan is feasible. Let's settle on it. Thank you, team.

lessons.title: War rooms & crisis meetings — operational
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma war room operacional em inglês simples — descreve o problema, define a causa, distribui responsáveis e marca o prazo das ações com a equipe interna.
lessons.overview:
A war room is a short, fast meeting. The team meets to solve one big problem on site. At Racional, a delay on a hospital or a data center can stop many other tasks. So the team needs to act fast. The war room helps the team stay calm and focused.

In a war room, the manager names the issue first. Then the team looks for the root cause. After that, the manager creates action items. Each action item has one owner and one deadline. This is simple, but it works. Everyone knows who does what and when.

For a contract manager, this skill is very important. American clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google work with clear plans. They want a recovery plan when something goes wrong. They want to be updated often. When you run a good war room in English, the client trusts your team and the project moves ASAP.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três estruturas-âncora que você vai usar na war room: "We have an issue with..." para abrir o problema, "The root cause is..." para apontar a causa e "Maria will... by Friday" para distribuir a ação com responsável e prazo.

Repare que cada ação tem um dono (owner) e um prazo (deadline). Em inglês simples, basta dizer o nome, o verbo e o dia.
lessons.situation: Há um atraso na entrega do concreto de uma laje no data center. Você reúne a equipe interna numa war room rápida para encontrar a causa e definir as ações urgentes antes de falar com o cliente.

We need a recovery plan now. Carlos will call the supplier this morning. Ana will check the schedule. I will keep the client updated. We must contain this delay ASAP. Let's meet again at five and follow up.

lessons.title: War rooms & crisis meetings — client-facing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma war room voltada ao cliente em inglês simples — comunica o problema com calma, assume a responsabilidade e apresenta o plano de correção ao cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you must give bad news to the client. A setback can happen on any project. The slab is late. A part does not arrive. A client-facing war room is the meeting where you talk about this with the client. The goal is simple: be calm, be clear, and show a plan.

American clients value transparency. They want you to be upfront and say the truth fast. They do not like surprises. When you take ownership of a problem, the client trusts you more. You say what went wrong, you say the impact, and you say how you will get back on track.

At Racional, this skill protects big contracts with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. A data center has a hard deadline. So you must reassure the client and show the corrective action. You also keep the client in the loop every day. With calm words and a clear plan, the client feels the project is under control.
lessons.intro:
Aqui a meta é falar com o cliente, não só com a equipe. Fixe três frases-âncora: "I want to be upfront with you." para abrir com transparência, "We take full ownership." para assumir a responsabilidade e "We have a plan to get back on track." para apresentar a correção.

Note o tom: calmo, honesto e com solução. Você tranquiliza (reassure) o cliente mostrando que está sob controle (under control).
lessons.situation: O atraso do concreto vai impactar um marco do data center. Você liga para o cliente americano em cima da hora (on short notice) para informar o problema, assumir a responsabilidade e apresentar o plano de correção.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time on short notice. I want to be upfront with you. We have a setback. The concrete was late. This may impact one milestone. We take full ownership of this. I want to reassure you. We have a corrective action. The new trucks come tomorrow. We will get back on track this week. The situation is under control. I will keep you in the loop every day. Rest assured, we are on it.

Thank you for the call on short notice.

lessons.title: American business media (WSJ, NYT, CNBC, Bloomberg)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconhece os principais veículos de mídia de negócios dos EUA (WSJ, NYT, CNBC, Bloomberg) e usa uma notícia recente como ponte para uma conversa leve com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
American business people read the news every day. They follow big outlets like the Wall Street Journal, the New York Times, CNBC, and Bloomberg. These outlets cover the economy, the markets, and big companies. A short headline can start a good talk before a meeting.

For you, the news is a bridge. You do not need to be an expert. You only need to skim one or two stories and know the main topic. Then you can ask a light question, like "What's your take?" American clients enjoy this. It shows you follow their world.

This small talk builds real trust. Microsoft, Amazon, and Google are in the news often. When you keep up with the markets and tech news, you connect with the client on a human level. Before a status update on a data center, two minutes about a recent headline can make the whole meeting warmer.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de relacionamento (bridge): o foco é a conexão, não a técnica de obra. Fixe três frases leves: "Did you see the news today?" para puxar assunto, "I read a piece on Bloomberg." para citar a fonte e "What's your take?" para devolver a palavra ao cliente.

O tom é casual. Você só precisa ter "passado o olho" (skim) numa notícia e mostrar interesse genuíno.
lessons.situation: Você espera o cliente americano entrar na sala virtual para o status semanal. Para quebrar o gelo, você comenta uma notícia recente de economia que leu de manhã.
lessons.context: Good morning! Did you see the news today? I follow the markets a little. This morning I read a piece on Bloomberg. The headline was about tech and data centers. I just skim the news with my coffee. I like to keep up with the economy. The WSJ and CNBC are good too. What's your take on the market this week? I always like to hear your view before we start.

lessons.title: Steering committees
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa de um steering committee em inglês — apresenta o status geral do contrato, reporta riscos e prazos e responde de forma clara aos diretores do cliente.
lessons.overview:
A steering committee is a high-level meeting. The sponsor and the directors of the client join it. They do not want every small detail. They want the big picture: is the project on track or behind schedule? This meeting often happens once a month.

In this meeting you give a clear status update. You talk about each milestone. You name the key risk. When a problem is too big for the team, you escalate it here. Sometimes you also ask for a sign-off or a decision. The leaders then say "go" and you proceed.

At Racional, steering committees keep big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google confident. On a data center contract, the sponsor wants to know the overall health of the project in two minutes. When you flag risks early and say what decision is needed, you show control. You also promise to keep them posted.
lessons.intro:
O steering committee é mais alto que a war room: aqui falam os patrocinadores e diretores. Fixe três frases-âncora: "Overall, the project is on track." para o status geral, "I want to flag one key risk." para o ponto de atenção e "We need a decision on this." para pedir o sign-off.

O tom é resumido e estratégico: visão geral, marco, risco, decisão. Pouco detalhe, muita clareza.
lessons.situation: É a reunião mensal do steering committee do data center. Os diretores do cliente americano querem o status geral, o próximo marco e os principais riscos do contrato.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. Here is the status update. Overall, the project is on track. The last milestone is done. The next milestone is the slab in June. I want to flag one key risk. The concrete supplier was slow last week. We have a plan, but I escalate it here. We also need a sign-off on the new design. This is the decision needed today. Once we have it, we proceed. I will keep you posted every week.

lessons.title: Negotiation fundamentals (BATNA, ZOPA)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa, em inglês, dois conceitos-chave de negociação — BATNA e ZOPA — para se preparar antes de negociar prazo, escopo ou custo com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before any talk about price or time, good managers prepare. Two ideas help a lot: BATNA and ZOPA. BATNA is your best alternative if there is no deal. It is your plan B. ZOPA is the zone where both sides can agree — the overlap between what you want and what the client wants.

Why does this matter? When you know your BATNA, you know when to walk away. You also know your bottom line — the lowest point you accept. When you find the ZOPA, you find common ground. Then both sides can give and take and reach an agreement.

At Racional, you negotiate scope, time, and cost with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. A small change on a data center can cost a lot. If you are prepared and know your leverage, you negotiate with calm. You protect the contract and you keep a good relationship with the client.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula é de preparação para negociar. Fixe três frases-âncora: "My BATNA is my best alternative." para o plano B, "Let's find common ground." para buscar a zona de acordo (ZOPA) e "This is our bottom line." para marcar o limite.

BATNA = melhor alternativa se não houver acordo. ZOPA = a faixa onde os dois lados podem fechar. Saber os dois te dá calma e poder (leverage).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede um prazo mais curto para um marco do data center. Antes da reunião, você se prepara: define sua melhor alternativa (BATNA) e a faixa possível de acordo (ZOPA).
lessons.context: Before the meeting, I prepare. I think about my BATNA. This is my best alternative. If there is no deal, I have a plan B. I also think about the ZOPA. This is the overlap, the common ground. The client wants a shorter time. We want a fair cost. There is a trade-off here. I know my bottom line. I am ready to give and take. But if it is too much, I can walk away. With a good plan, we reach an agreement.

vocab.pt: melhor alternativa caso não haja acordo
vocab.example: My BATNA is my plan B.
The ZOPA is where we agree.
We want to reach an agreement.
I can walk away if needed.
I am prepared for the talk.

options.whyWrong: Isso entrega a negociação; o objetivo é marcar o limite, não abrir mão de tudo.

exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos. O objetivo é mostrar que você se preparou antes de negociar.

lessons.title: Negotiation tactics & language
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa táticas e linguagem de negociação em inglês — ancorar, fazer e pedir concessões e propor com 'if you... then I...' — para conduzir uma negociação de escopo ou prazo com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In a real negotiation, you use simple tactics. First you anchor: you make the first opening offer. This sets the start point. Then both sides move. You give a concession, and you ask for one back. The goal is a win-win, where both sides are happy.

Good language helps you stay calm. You can push back in a polite way. You can hold firm on an important point. You can also meet halfway or split the difference on price. When you need more time, you say "Let me get back to you." When you agree, you say "Just to confirm..."

At Racional, you use these tactics on scope and price with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. A change on a data center is a package deal: time, cost, and quality move together. You trade one thing in exchange for another. You also know your deal-breaker — the one point you cannot accept.
lessons.intro:
Aqui você passa da preparação para a mesa. Fixe três frases-âncora: "Let me make an opening offer." para ancorar, "If you accept X, then I can offer Y." para a troca condicional e "Let's meet halfway." para fechar no meio do caminho.

Lembre da lógica da troca: toda concessão sua vem com um pedido (in exchange for). E saiba seu deal-breaker — o ponto que não dá para ceder.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano quer adiantar a entrega de um marco e baixar o custo. Você conduz a negociação: ancora a proposta, faz trocas condicionais e busca um acordo win-win.
lessons.context: Thank you. Let me make an opening offer. We can move the deadline by one week. But this has a cost. If you accept the extra cost, then I can add more workers. This is a fair trade-off. I can give some ground here, in exchange for a longer payment term. Let's meet halfway on the price. A late penalty is a deal-breaker for us. So let's keep it out. Just to confirm: one week earlier, more workers, same quality. I think this is a win-win. Let me get back to you tomorrow with the final number.

vocab.example: I will anchor with a first offer.
Let me make an opening offer.
Let's meet halfway on the price.
The client may counter my offer.
I give time in exchange for cost.
I hold firm on safety rules.
I can give some ground here.
Let me get back to you tomorrow.
Just to confirm, one week earlier.
I push back on the short time.
I think this is a win-win.

lessons.title: Hard bargaining vs. principled negotiation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue, em inglês simples, diferenciar a negociação dura da negociação por princípios e usar frases para focar em interesses e critérios justos com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you can play it hard or play it fair. Hard bargaining means you push your position and you do not move. It can work one time, but it can hurt the relationship. As a contract manager at Racional, you work with the same client for many months. A bad win today can cost you tomorrow.

Principled negotiation is a better way. You do not fight over positions. You look at the real interest behind each position. You use a fair and clear rule, like a market price or a standard, to decide. This is very useful with North American clients, because they like clear numbers and clear logic.

On a big project, like a data center for Microsoft or Amazon, the client and Racional must talk many times about cost, scope, and time. You will not agree on everything. But if you stay calm and look for a fair answer, you and the client part on good terms. The goal is a deal that works for both sides, today and for the whole project.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai treinar a sair da "queda de braço" e ir para uma negociação por princípios. Relembre três âncoras: "Let's look at the real interest here" (vamos olhar o interesse real), "Let's use a fair benchmark" (vamos usar um critério justo) e "It's not personal — let's find a fair answer".

A ideia central: separe a pessoa do problema, foque no interesse por trás da posição e decida com base em algo justo e mensurável.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de obra, o cliente americano abre uma posição dura sobre prazo. Em vez de bater de frente, você busca o interesse real dele e propõe um critério justo.
lessons.context: The client wants a faster date. That is his position. But the real interest is a safe opening day. So I do not fight. I ask about the real need. Then I offer a fair plan based on the real work. We do not take it personally. We find a fair answer, and we part on good terms.

vocab.example: Hard bargaining can hurt the relationship.

The real interest is a safe site.
I try to soften the tone.
We use a fair benchmark for the price.
I want to de-escalate the meeting.

I do not take it personally.

lessons.title: Music talk 5: building rapport through music
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue, em inglês simples, usar a música como tema de conversa para criar conexão (rapport) com clientes e parceiros internacionais.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. It is easy, it is friendly, and almost everyone likes some kind of music. When you talk about a song or a band, you break the ice fast. This is your fifth and last Music Talk lesson. You started with Seal, your go-to artist, and you also talked about Sade, Lenny Kravitz, and Jamiroquai.

For a contract manager at Racional, this skill is very useful. A big project can last 18 to 24 months. You meet the same client many times — in meetings, in lunches, in trips. Small talk about music helps you build rapport and bond over a shared taste. People remember a warm, human talk, not only the numbers.

North American clients often enjoy this light talk before and after the formal meeting. You can ask what they like, share a playlist, or recommend a song. You do not need perfect English. You need real interest and a few simple questions. That is how you turn a work contact into a long, friendly relationship.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula-ponte o foco é conexão, não gramática. Relembre três âncoras leves: "What music are you into these days?" (que música você curte hoje em dia?), "We have that in common" (temos isso em comum) e "I'll send you a playlist" (vou te mandar uma playlist).

Tom leve e curioso. O objetivo é quebrar o gelo e criar vínculo com o cliente.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião com o cliente americano, há cinco minutos de conversa. Você usa a música para criar um clima leve e fortalecer a relação.
lessons.context: Before the meeting, we have a few minutes. I ask the client about music. He likes soul and funk. We have that in common. I tell him about Seal, my go-to artist. We bond over the same songs. At the end, I say: I'll send you a playlist. It is a small thing, but it builds rapport.

lessons.title: Pricing negotiations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue, em inglês simples, conduzir uma conversa sobre preço — explicar o custo, mostrar valor e segurar o preço com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Price talk is part of every project. The client always wants a lower price. You want a fair price that covers the real cost. A good contract manager does not just say a number. You walk the client through the cost. You show what is inside the price. This builds trust.

At Racional, the price must reflect the real value of the work — the quality, the safety, the experience of 50 years and 620+ projects. When the client sees the full cost breakdown, the price makes sense. You can show that Racional is competitive and still gives strong value for money.

Sometimes you must hold the price. Some items are non-negotiable, like safety. With North American clients, clear numbers help a lot. You explain the scope, you show the margin is fair, and you offer options, like a discount on volume or a phased plan. The goal is a price both sides can accept.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você treina a defender um preço com calma e clareza. Relembre três âncoras: "Let me walk you through the cost" (deixe-me explicar o custo), "This price reflects the value" (este preço reflete o valor) e "This item is non-negotiable" (este item não é negociável).

A lógica: mostre o que está dentro do preço, ligue preço a valor e segure o que não pode cair (como segurança).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede desconto. Você não corta na hora: você explica o custo, mostra o valor e segura o que é essencial.
lessons.context: The client asks for a lower price. I stay calm. I say: let me walk you through the cost. I show the cost breakdown. The price reflects the quality and the safety. We are competitive. I can offer a small discount on volume. But safety is non-negotiable. I hold the price on that part.

lessons.title: Scope negotiations & change orders
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue, em inglês simples, negociar uma mudança de escopo (change order) com o cliente — dizer o que está dentro ou fora do escopo e pedir aprovação por escrito.
lessons.overview:
Every project starts with a clear scope. The scope is the list of work in the contract. Some work is in scope. Other work is out of scope. When the client wants new work, that is a change order. As a contract manager, you must say this clearly and early.

A common risk is scope creep. This is when small extra tasks are added, little by little, with no clear deal. On a big job, like a hospital or a data center, scope creep can hurt cost and time. So at Racional you protect the baseline — the agreed plan — and you control every change.

The rule is simple: every change needs a cost impact and a schedule impact, and it must be in writing. You quote the extra work, the client approves it, and only then you start. North American clients respect this clear process. It protects both sides and keeps the relationship strong.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você treina a controlar mudanças de escopo. Relembre três âncoras: "That is out of scope" (isso está fora do escopo), "This change has a cost and schedule impact" (esta mudança impacta custo e prazo) e "I need it in writing" (preciso por escrito).

A lógica: defina in/out de escopo, mostre o impacto de cada change order e nunca comece sem aprovação por escrito.
lessons.situation: Na obra, o cliente americano pede um item novo que não estava no contrato. Você trata como change order: aponta o escopo, o impacto e pede aprovação formal.
lessons.context: The client asks for a new wall. That is out of scope. It is not in the contract. So I treat it as a change order. I explain the cost impact and the schedule impact. lessons.title: Deadline negotiations & timeline extensions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue, em inglês simples, negociar prazo com o cliente — dizer se a obra está no prazo ou atrasada e propor um plano de recuperação.
lessons.overview:
Time is one of the biggest topics on any project. The client always asks one thing: are we on track or behind schedule? As a contract manager, you must answer with honest, simple words. A clear answer about time builds trust.

Every project has key dates, called milestones, and one final handover date. Some tasks are on the critical path. If they are late, the whole project is late. At Racional, on a fast project like a data center for Amazon or Google, you watch these dates every day. You also keep a small buffer for risk.

Sometimes there is a delay, and you need to ask for an extension. The key is to be transparent. You explain the cause, you show a clear recovery plan, and you say how you will make up time. North American clients accept bad news better when you bring a plan, not just a problem.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você treina a falar de prazo com clareza. Relembre três âncoras: "We are on track" / "We are behind schedule", "We have a recovery plan" (temos um plano de recuperação) e "We can make up time here" (podemos recuperar tempo aqui).

A lógica: diga a verdade sobre o status, mostre os milestones em risco e traga sempre um plano para recuperar.
lessons.situation: Na reunião semanal, o cliente americano pergunta sobre o prazo. Há um pequeno atraso e você apresenta o status com transparência e um plano de recuperação.
lessons.context: We are a little behind schedule. One milestone is late. It is on the critical path. I am transparent about it. But I have a recovery plan. We will add a team and make up time next week. I ask for a short extension on the handover. With the plan, we can get back on track.

lessons.title: Difficult conversations & conflict resolution
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue, em inglês simples, conduzir uma conversa difícil e resolver um conflito com o cliente ou um fornecedor — levantar o problema com calma e buscar um caminho comum.
lessons.overview:
On any project, problems happen. A supplier is late. A cost goes up. The client is not happy. Then you must have a difficult conversation. Many people avoid it, but a good contract manager does not. You raise the issue early, with calm and respect.

The key is how you talk. You do not blame the other person. You stay honest and you focus on the problem, not the people. You look for common ground — the things you both want. At Racional, with a North American client, this clear and respectful style keeps trust strong, even in a hard moment.

The goal is a way forward, not a winner and a loser. You address the real issue, you clear the air, and you make sure both sides are on the same page. When you handle conflict well, the relationship gets stronger, not weaker. That is real leadership on a long project.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você treina a conduzir conversas difíceis. Relembre três âncoras: "I'd like to raise an issue" (gostaria de levantar um ponto), "I'm concerned about this" (estou preocupado com isso) e "Let's find a way forward" (vamos achar um caminho).

A lógica: levante o problema cedo, fale com honestidade sem culpar, e busque um terreno comum e um caminho à frente.
lessons.situation: Um fornecedor entregou material com atraso e o cliente está incomodado. Você conduz a conversa com calma, sem culpar, buscando uma solução.
lessons.context: I need a difficult conversation with the supplier. I stay calm. I say: I'd like to raise an issue. I'm concerned about the delay. I am honest, but I do not blame him. I focus on the problem. We look for common ground. Together we find a way forward. We clear the air and we are on the same page.

I want to be honest with you.

lessons.title: US construction industry landscape
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, sobre como funciona o setor de construção nos Estados Unidos — os papéis, os termos e a cultura de segurança — para criar conexão com o cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
This is a BRIDGE lesson. It is lighter. Today you learn about the construction industry in the United States. Most clients of Racional are from the US. When you know their world, you build a strong connection. You stop being only a supplier. You become a real partner.

In the US, the general contractor runs the whole job. This role is like Racional. The general contractor hires many subcontractors. Each subcontractor does one trade, like electrical or plumbing. Safety is very important. The federal agency is called OSHA. On every jobsite, workers wear safety gear and follow strict rules. The motto is simple: safety first.

Your big clients are hyperscalers. Microsoft, Amazon, and Google build huge data centers. For these clients, the goal is always the same. The project must be on time and on budget. Racional builds these data centers in Brazil. So when you talk about general contractors, OSHA, and safety, the American client sees you as an equal. This is real rapport.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, mais leve. Você vai usar termos do setor americano: general contractor, subcontractor, OSHA e safety first.

Frases-âncora desta aula: "We run the job." (Nós tocamos a obra.) e "Safety is first." (Segurança em primeiro lugar.)
lessons.situation: Num almoço informal, o cliente americano comenta como as obras funcionam nos EUA. Você mostra que conhece o setor dele e a conversa flui.
lessons.context: In the US, the general contractor runs the job. The general contractor hires the subs. Each sub does one trade. Safety is very important. OSHA makes the rules. Everyone wears safety gear. The goal is on time and on budget. It is a lot like Brazil.

lessons.title: Saying no diplomatically
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz "não" de forma diplomática ao cliente ou a um fornecedor em inglês simples — recusando um pedido com respeito, dando o motivo e oferecendo uma alternativa.
lessons.overview:
Today you learn to say no in a polite way. This is a key skill for a contract manager. A hard "no" closes the door. A polite "no" protects the job and the relationship. On a real jobsite, you cannot say yes to everything. Sometimes the request is not feasible. Sometimes it is not safe. You must say no, but with respect.

The polite no has three simple parts. First, you show you understand. You say "I'm afraid..." or "Unfortunately...". Second, you give the reason. Maybe it is a constraint of time, cost, or safety. Third, you offer an alternative. You say "What I can do is...". You almost never say the word "no" alone.

At Racional, the American client often asks for more speed or less cost. You want to help. But you must be realistic. You cannot compromise on safety. So you explain the trade-off in clear words, and you always end with a solution. The client remembers the door you opened, not the door you closed. This builds trust on every Microsoft, Amazon, or Google project.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você recusa sem fechar a porta. A fórmula tem três partes: reconhecer, dar o motivo, oferecer alternativa.

Frases-âncora: "I'm afraid that is not possible." (Infelizmente isso não é possível.) e "What I can do is..." (O que eu posso fazer é...). Nunca termine no "não" — termine no que você pode fazer.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede para antecipar a entrega de uma área em duas semanas, o que comprometeria a segurança. Você recusa com diplomacia e oferece uma alternativa segura.
lessons.context: I understand why you ask. Unfortunately, two weeks earlier is not feasible. It is a safety risk, and we cannot compromise on safety. What I can do is deliver this section first. Then you can start your work there.

lessons.title: Disagreeing & pushing back politely
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você discorda do cliente ou de um colega em inglês simples — apresentando um ponto de vista diferente com respeito, sem soar agressivo e sem ceder ao que sabe estar errado.
lessons.overview:
Today you learn to disagree in a polite way. A contract manager does not agree with everything. Sometimes the client is wrong about a date, a cost, or a technical choice. You must say it, but with respect. This is called pushing back. You stand your ground, but you keep the relationship strong.

The secret is simple. First, you show respect. You say "I see your point" or "Fair point". This is important for American clients. They like a clear opinion, but they want respect too. Then you add your view with one word: "however". After that, you give your reason. The best reason is data. You say "the data shows..." or "from my experience...".

At Racional, you push back every week. The client wants a faster schedule. The design has a risk. A supplier is late. You cannot just say yes. You raise a concern, you show the facts, and you ask the client to reconsider. On a Microsoft or Amazon data center, one wrong choice costs a lot. So a polite, clear pushback is not a fight. It protects the project and your name.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você discorda com respeito. A estrutura é: concordar um pouco, virar com "however", apoiar no dado.

Frases-âncora: "I see your point, however..." (Entendo seu ponto, porém...) e "The data shows..." (Os dados mostram...). Discordar não é brigar — é proteger a obra.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de status, o cliente americano insiste num prazo que você sabe que é arriscado. Você discorda com respeito e mostra o dado.
lessons.context: I see your point. However, my concern is the safety risk. From my experience, this date is too tight. The data shows we need three more days. I'd suggest we move the date a little.

lessons.title: Persuasion & influencing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você convence o cliente ou um colega de uma ideia em inglês simples — mostrando o benefício, apoiando no dado e conseguindo o "sim".
lessons.overview:
Today you learn to persuade people in English. A contract manager has good ideas every day. A better method, a safer plan, a smarter date. But a good idea is not enough. You must make the case. You must convince the client and your team. Persuasion is not pressure. It is a clear, calm way to show value.

The key is simple. You show the benefit for the other person. You do not say "this is good for me". You say "the benefit for you is...". People say yes when they see what they win. Then you back it up with data or an example. Data makes your idea compelling. After that, you ask for the next step. You want the client to be on board.

At Racional, you persuade all the time. You want the client to approve a change, a new supplier, or a safer method. The best result is win-win: good for the client, good for the project. When you speak with a Microsoft or Amazon team, you must sound confident and clear. A strong, simple case in English helps you get buy-in and move the data center forward.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você convence mostrando o benefício para o outro. A estrutura é: benefício + dado + próximo passo.

Frases-âncora: "The benefit for you is..." (O benefício para você é...) e "Let me back it up." (Deixe-me apoiar com dado.). Foco no que o cliente ganha.
lessons.situation: Você quer que o cliente americano aprove um método mais seguro de execução. Você mostra o benefício para ele e o dado.
lessons.context: I recommend a new method. The benefit for you is more safety and no delay. The data backs it up. It is a win-win. Are you on board? The next step is a quick test on site.

lessons.title: Presenting proposals & defending positions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta uma proposta e defende sua posição em inglês simples — recomendando uma solução, dando o motivo e respondendo a objeções com calma.
lessons.overview:
Today you learn to present a proposal and defend a position. A contract manager often presents a plan to the client. A new schedule, a new supplier, a change in the design. You must explain your idea in clear English. Then you must defend it when the client asks hard questions. This is a key skill in every status meeting.

A good proposal has a simple shape. You start with the recommendation: "I recommend...". Then you give the reason: "The reason is...". You back it up with data. When the client pushes back, you stay calm. You say "I understand your point", and then you stand by your view with respect. If needed, you offer an alternative or you name the trade-off.

At Racional, you defend positions every week. The client wants a cheaper option, but it has a risk. You present your proposal, you show the data, and you explain the bottom line. On a Microsoft, Amazon, or Google data center, the schedule and the cost are huge. So a clear, calm defense of a good idea protects the whole project. You sound like a strong partner, not a weak supplier.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você apresenta e defende uma proposta. A estrutura é: recomendação + motivo + dado, e calma na objeção.

Frases-âncora: "I recommend..." (Eu recomendo...), "The reason is..." (O motivo é...) e "I understand your point, but..." (Entendo seu ponto, mas...).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de status, você propõe um novo fornecedor para uma frente crítica. O cliente questiona, e você defende sua posição com dado.
lessons.context: I recommend a new supplier. The reason is better quality and the same cost. I understand your point about the change. However, the data backs it up. The bottom line is less risk for the project.

lessons.title: Travel stories & destinations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta histórias de viagem e fala sobre destinos com o cliente em inglês simples — uma das conversas mais fáceis e calorosas para criar vínculo num jantar ou num voo.
lessons.overview:
This is a BRIDGE lesson. Relax. Today you talk about travel and destinations. On a long project, you travel with the client. You have dinner together. You wait at airports. And almost everyone loves to talk about trips. Travel is the easiest and warmest topic for small talk.

You need two simple questions. The first is "Have you been to...?". The second is "What is your favorite place?". Then you tell a short story of your own. Where you went, what you saw, what you loved. You do not need advanced English. Three short sentences are enough: "Last year I went to Portugal. The local food was great. I loved it."

At Racional, your projects last 18 to 24 months. So you build long relationships with the American client and the international team. Travel talk is a great door. You can recommend a place in Brazil. You can ask about their last trip. You show curiosity, you smile, and the connection grows. A small, warm talk today makes the next meeting easier tomorrow.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, relaxe. Você vai puxar conversa sobre viagens e contar uma história curta sua.

Frases-âncora: "Have you been to...?" (Você já foi a...?) e "Last year I went to..." (Ano passado eu fui a...). Conte uma história e devolva a pergunta.
lessons.situation: Jantar com o cliente americano depois de uma visita à obra. A conversa esfria. Você puxa o assunto de viagens e conta de uma viagem que marcou você.
lessons.context: Have you been to Brazil before? You should see the coast. The beaches are stunning. Last year I went to Portugal on vacation. The local food was great and the people were friendly. What is your favorite place to travel?

lessons.title: Phone calls & voicemails
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir atender e fazer ligações simples em inglês, deixar e entender recados de voz com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
On a big project, the phone never stops. A voicemail from an American client can hold an urgent question about a deadline, a cost, or a safety issue. As a contract manager at Racional, you call suppliers, clients, and your own team every day. Clear phone English keeps the work moving.

On the phone you cannot see the other person. You cannot point at a drawing or a wall. So your words must be simple and clear. You say your name. You say why you call. If the line is bad, you ask the person to speak slowly or to repeat that. This is normal, and it is professional.

For data center clients like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, a fast call back shows control. When you cannot answer, you leave a message with your name, the date, and a short reason. A good voicemail saves time and builds trust. Phone English is small, but it is part of running the contract well.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai praticar três âncoras de telefone: "This is Fernando from Racional." (para se identificar), "I'm calling about the schedule." (para dizer o motivo) e "Could you repeat that, please?" (quando não entender).

Use frases curtas. No telefone, clareza vale mais que vocabulário difícil.
