lessons.title: Closing meetings & next steps
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir fechar uma reunião em inglês: resumir, definir próximos passos e dizer quem é responsável por cada tarefa.
lessons.overview:
The last two minutes of a meeting are the most important. This is when you say what you decided and who does what. A clear close stops confusion later. As a contract manager at Racional, you run many meetings with clients and suppliers, and a good close keeps the project on track.

To close well, you recap the main points. Then you list the next steps. Each step has an owner and a deadline. You say, "John is in charge of the report. The deadline is Friday." Now everyone knows the plan. No one says later, "I did not know that was my job."

For American clients like Amazon or Google, this habit is normal and expected. They like clear action items and a short summary. When you follow up the next day, you look organized and in control. A strong meeting close is a small skill with a big result on a large data center job.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai praticar o fechamento de reunião com três âncoras: "Let me recap." (para resumir), "The next step is..." (para os próximos passos) e "You are in charge of this." (para definir responsável).

Sempre ligue cada tarefa a um responsável e a um prazo.

lessons.title: Follow-up emails & meeting recaps
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir escrever um e-mail simples de follow-up com o resumo da reunião e os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
After a meeting, the talking stops, but the work goes on. A short follow-up email writes down what you decided. It is the proof of the meeting. As a contract manager at Racional, this email protects you. If there is a question later, the email has the answer.

A good recap email is short and clear. You start with "As discussed," then you list the points. You name the outstanding items and who owns each one. You can attach a file, like the schedule or the safety report. You end with a polite line and ask people to reply if something is missing.

For American clients like Microsoft or Google, writing things down is part of the culture. A clear email after the call shows you are organized. It helps you confirm in writing the dates, the costs, and the actions. On a big data center job, this simple habit prevents big problems.

Nesta aula você vai praticar três âncoras de e-mail: "As discussed, here is a recap." (abertura), "Please find the report below." (anexo/conteúdo) e "Let me know if I missed anything." (fechamento).

O e-mail de follow-up é curto: abertura, lista de pontos e pedido de retorno.

lessons.title: Cross-cultural meeting etiquette
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai entender o estilo de reunião norte-americano e conseguir participar de forma direta e educada.
lessons.overview:
Every country has its own meeting style. American clients like to be on time and they like to get to the point. They keep a short agenda and they want to make a decision at the end. For a Racional contract manager, knowing this style helps you work well with clients like Amazon and Google.

In American meetings, people are direct, but they are still polite. "Direct" does not mean rude. It means clear. They say what they think in simple words. They do not talk for a long time before the main point. They like to stay on track and follow the agenda. A little small talk at the start is normal, then the work begins.

When two people disagree, Americans often say, "Let's take it offline." This means "we will talk about it later, just us two." Being on the same page is the goal: everyone understands the same thing. When you learn this style, your meetings feel smooth, and you come across as a clear and professional partner.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai praticar três âncoras culturais: "Let's get started." (para começar), "Let's get to the point." (para ir direto) e "Are we on the same page?" (para alinhar).

Lembre: ser direto em inglês é ser claro, não ser grosseiro.

We can take the cost issue offline. At the end, we will make a decision. Are we all on the same page? Great. Thank you.

lessons.title: US safety & OSHA culture
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conhecer a cultura de segurança dos EUA e a OSHA, e conseguir falar sobre segurança com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, safety is not just a rule; it is a culture. The word you hear most on a job site is "safety first." American companies put safety at the top, even before speed and cost. For a Racional contract manager, knowing this culture builds trust with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google.

The big name in US safety is OSHA. It is a government agency that makes safety rules for work sites. On site, workers wear PPE: a hard hat, glasses, and boots. Every day there is a short toolbox talk about the risks of the day. These rules are mandatory, which means everyone must follow them.

When something almost goes wrong, it is a near miss. People report it, even if no one is hurt. The goal is simple: zero accidents. American clients value this a lot. When you talk about your safety briefing and your low number of incidents, you show that Racional shares the same culture. This builds a strong relationship.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de relacionamento e cultura. Você vai conversar sobre segurança com leveza, mostrando que a Racional valoriza o mesmo que o cliente.

Âncoras: "Safety is our top priority." e "We had zero accidents this month."
lessons.situation: Numa visita à obra, o cliente americano pergunta sobre suas práticas de segurança. Você quer mostrar que a Racional leva isso a sério.
lessons.context: Safety is our top priority. Every morning we have a short toolbox talk. All workers wear PPE: a hard hat, glasses, and boots. The rules are mandatory. If we see a near miss, we report it. Our goal is zero accidents. We follow the safety briefing every day. This month we had no lost-time injuries. Safety first, always.

lessons.title: Tropicalização in meetings: explaining BR realities
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir explicar ao cliente, em inglês simples, as realidades locais do Brasil e propor soluções práticas.
lessons.overview:
Brazil is not the United States, and a good plan must fit the local reality. Lead times are longer. Some materials must be imported. The rainy season can stop outdoor work for days. As a Racional contract manager, your job is to explain these constraints to the client in a clear and calm way.

This is called tropicalização: you adapt a global plan to the Brazilian site. You do not change the standard; you find a smart way to meet the same standard here. For example, if one part has a long lead time, you find a local supplier or a good workaround to keep the project on schedule.

American clients like Amazon and Google respect honesty. When you explain a constraint early and bring a solution, you build trust. You are not making excuses; you are showing local knowledge. This is the real value of Racional: 50 years of building in Brazil, and the skill to adapt a hyperscale data center to local conditions without losing quality.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai praticar como explicar uma realidade local e já trazer a solução. Âncoras: "This is a local constraint.", "We have a workaround." e "We will keep the project on schedule."

Regra de ouro: explique o problema e, na mesma fala, ofereça a saída.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião, você precisa explicar ao cliente americano que um equipamento tem prazo longo de importação e propor uma alternativa local.
lessons.context: I want to explain a local constraint. This part is imported, so the lead time is long. The rainy season can also slow us down. But we have a workaround. We will use a local supplier for some items. It will meet the same standard. This way, we keep the project on schedule. I will confirm the dates this week.

lessons.title: Storytelling em reuniões
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta uma história curta numa reunião — um problema na obra e como a equipe resolveu — para deixar o status mais claro e marcante para o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In meetings, numbers are useful. But a short story is easy to remember. When you tell the client how your team fixed a problem, you show skill. You do not need to talk a lot. Three short sentences are enough. This is called storytelling, and it works well in a status update.

A good site story has three parts. First, the problem. Then the action of the team. In the end, the outcome. For example: a supplier was late, the team found a local option, and you recovered the schedule. This is real and clear. It is not a long speech.

At Racional, your clients are often from the United States — big names like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. They build data centers and want fast answers. A simple story shows that your team can react fast and stay calm. It builds trust, and trust keeps the project strong for many months.
lessons.intro:
Lembre a estrutura de três passos que vamos usar: "Last week, we had a problem..." (problema), "So the team..." (ação) e "In the end, we..." (resultado).

Use o passado simples (found, fixed, worked) e frases curtas. Problema, ação, resultado: três frases já contam uma história forte.
lessons.situation: Status update semanal com o cliente norte-americano. Em vez de só listar números, você conta rápido como a equipe resolveu um atraso de fornecedor na semana passada.
lessons.context: Last week, we had a problem. A supplier was late. So the team reacted fast. We found a local option in two days. In the end, we recovered the schedule. We also kept the quality. It was a real challenge, but we pulled it off.

I can use the simple past to say what the team did.

lessons.title: Executive summaries & reporting up
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz um resumo executivo curto — panorama, risco e ação — para reportar ao cliente ou à diretoria de forma direta.
lessons.overview:
An executive summary is your status in a few short sentences. You start with the most important point. Directors are busy. They do not have time for a long report. So you give the bottom line first, and then the details. This is the smart way to report up to senior people.

A safe summary has three blocks. First, the big picture: overall, the project is on track. Then the risk: one key point needs attention. In the end, the action: the team is already on it. Each milestone and each cost is under control. You wrap up in two minutes, with no major issues hidden.

At Racional, this skill is very useful in monthly meetings with American clients like Amazon or Google. They run huge data center projects and check progress often. A clear summary shows control. It saves time and builds trust. Good news first, then the risk with the plan — that is the headline they want to hear.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora: "Overall, the project is on track." (panorama), "One risk is..." (ponto de atenção) e "We are handling it." (ação).

Comece pela conclusão, não pelo histórico. E nunca apresente um problema sem dizer o que você está fazendo a respeito.
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal com a diretoria do cliente norte-americano. Você tem dois minutos para resumir o andamento antes das perguntas.
lessons.context: Overall, the project is on track. We are at sixty percent. The bottom line is good. One key point is the steel delivery. But we are handling it with a local supplier. Cost is under control. We hit the last milestone on time. In short, no major issues this month.

lessons.title: Email writing — formal vs. casual
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você escolhe entre um e-mail formal e um casual — e usa as frases prontas certas — para escrever ao cliente norte-americano com o tom adequado.
lessons.overview:
Email is a big part of your day. But not every email is the same. Some are formal, for a new client or a contract. Some are casual, for a colleague you know well. The same message can have two tones. The smart manager picks the right one. A clear subject line and the right opening make a strong first impression.

A formal email starts with Dear ... and ends with Best regards. You write I am writing to ... and Please find attached the file. A casual email starts with Hi or Hello and ends with Thanks. You can touch base with a quick note. Both are correct. The tone just changes with the recipient.

At Racional, your clients are often from the United States. With companies like Microsoft or Amazon, the first emails are usually formal. Later, when you know the team, the tone gets lighter. Knowing both tones helps you sound right. It shows respect, and it keeps the long data center project moving in a smooth way.
lessons.intro:
Guarde duas aberturas e dois fechamentos: formal "Dear Mr. Smith / Best regards" e casual "Hi John / Thanks".

E duas frases muito úteis: "Please find attached..." (segue anexo) e "Please let me know..." (me avise). A regra é simples: o tom segue o destinatário.
lessons.situation: Você precisa enviar dois e-mails: um formal para um novo diretor do cliente e um rápido para um colega de equipe que você já conhece bem.
lessons.context: Dear Mr. Smith, I am writing to confirm the meeting on Monday. Please find attached the report. Please let me know if you have questions. Best regards, Fernando. And to a colleague: Hi John, just a quick note to touch base. Thanks!

lessons.title: Birthdays, anniversaries & milestones
lessons.objective: Nesta aula-ponte (BRIDGE), mais leve, você parabeniza pessoas e fala sobre datas especiais — aniversários, datas da empresa e marcos da obra — para criar vínculo com clientes e parceiros.
lessons.overview:
A long project is not only about work. It is also about people. When you remember a birthday or an anniversary, you show that you care. A short, warm message means a lot. You do not need a big speech. One kind sentence is enough to celebrate the moment and mark the occasion.

There are three special dates to know. A birthday is for a person. An anniversary is for a company or an event, like one year of the project. A milestone is a big step, like finishing a floor on site. For each one, you have an easy phrase: Happy birthday!, Congratulations!, and Congrats on this milestone! You can also wish someone all the best.

At Racional, projects run for eighteen to twenty-four months. You see the same American client team for a long time. A friendly word on a special day builds a real bond. It is small talk that creates trust. So when the team finishes a big achievement, raise a glass and say Cheers! — it keeps the relationship warm.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, mais leve, para criar conexão humana. Guarde as frases prontas: "Happy birthday!", "Congratulations!" e "Congrats on this milestone!".

Cuidado com a diferença: birthday é de pessoa; anniversary é de empresa ou evento. Trocar os dois é o erro mais comum.
lessons.situation: A obra do cliente norte-americano completa um ano. No almoço, o gerente do cliente também faz aniversário. Você quer parabenizar nas duas situações com naturalidade.
lessons.context: Happy birthday! I hope you have a great day. And congratulations on the project anniversary — one year already! This is a big milestone for the whole team. Well done to everyone. Let's celebrate. Cheers to the team!

vocab.example: I wish you all the best.
Time to blow out the candles.
We meet to mark the occasion.
Many happy returns of the day.

exercises.modelAnswer: Happy birthday! I wish you all the best. And congratulations on this big milestone. Let's celebrate this achievement together.
exercises.explanation: Curto e caloroso: parabéns pela pessoa e pelo marco, com tom sincero.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15 a 20 segundos, parabenize um cliente por um marco da obra e por uma data pessoal. Use 'milestone' e uma frase de parabéns.
takeaways: I can wish someone a happy birthday.
I can use 'anniversary' for a company or an event.
I can say congratulations on a milestone.
I can write a short, warm message to mark the occasion.

lessons.title: Email — escalations & complaints
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você escreve um e-mail firme e educado para escalar um problema — um atraso de fornecedor — pedindo ação e uma data sem perder o tom profissional.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a problem does not stop. A supplier is late again. A part does not arrive. In these cases, you need to escalate. To escalate means to take the problem to a higher level, in a firm but polite way. A good escalation email is clear. It says the matter, the impact, and the firm date you need. It stays professional, never angry.

The structure is simple. First, you raise a concern: a delay is real. Then the impact: it can put the schedule at risk. Then the request: you expect action and need urgent attention. You can write that the situation is unacceptable, but you stay calm. You close with I appreciate your support and ask to follow up by a clear date.

At Racional, this skill protects the project. American clients like Microsoft and Google have tight deadlines on data centers. When a vendor fails, a firm email as agreed can take action fast and save the schedule. Firm words and a polite tone work together. You defend the deadline, and you keep the relationship strong.
lessons.intro:
Relembre o esqueleto do e-mail de escalada: "I am writing to raise a concern about the delay." (problema), "This puts the schedule at risk." (impacto) e "We need a firm date and urgent attention." (pedido).

O segredo é ser firme e educado ao mesmo tempo: feche com "I appreciate your support."
lessons.situation: Um fornecedor já atrasou duas vezes e isso ameaça o prazo da obra. Você escreve um e-mail firme, mas educado, pedindo uma data definitiva e ação imediata.
lessons.context: Dear Mr. Lee, I am writing to raise a concern about the delay. This is the second delay. It puts the schedule at risk. This is unacceptable. We need a firm date and urgent attention. Please take action as agreed. I appreciate your support.

lessons.title: Meeting minutes & action tracking
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você registra a ata de uma reunião com itens de ação — responsável e prazo — e acompanha o que está feito, em andamento ou pendente.
lessons.overview:
A meeting is only useful if people act after it. So you write meeting minutes: a short record of what the team decided. The most important part is the list of action items. Each action item has an owner (the person) and a due date (the deadline). Without an owner and a date, nothing happens.

After the meeting, you track the work. You assign each task and check the status. A task can be done, in progress, or pending. If a task is late, it is overdue — you flag it fast. You also record each decision, so no one forgets later. This keeps the project clear for everyone.

At Racional, this is daily work on site. In meetings with American clients like Amazon or Microsoft, clear minutes prevent confusion. The client sees the owner, the deadline, and the status of each follow-up. It shows control and trust. Good minutes turn a long meeting into clear action, and clear action keeps the data center project on time.
lessons.intro:
Relembre o trio de uma boa ata: o action item (a tarefa), o owner (quem faz) e a due date (até quando).

E os três status que você vai usar para acompanhar: "done" (feito), "in progress" (em andamento) e "pending" (pendente).
lessons.situation: Após a reunião semanal com o cliente, você envia a ata com os itens de ação. Cada item tem um responsável e um prazo, e você marca o status de cada um.
lessons.context: Here are the meeting minutes. Action item one: order the steel. Owner: Paulo. Due date: Friday. Status: in progress. Action item two: send the report. Owner: Ana. This one is done. Item three is still pending. We will track all of them.

lessons.title: Site visit em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conduzir uma visita à obra em inglês, mostrando áreas, apontando o que está pronto e dando avisos de segurança.
lessons.overview:
A site visit is a normal day for a contract manager at Racional. The client comes to the construction site. You walk with the client. You show the work. You explain what is done and what is in progress. North American clients like clear and short words. They want to see real progress with their own eyes.

On a data center project for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, the site visit is very important. The client checks the slab, the floors, and the structure. You guide the visit. You say "follow me" and "over here". You point out the new areas. You also keep everyone safe with a hard hat and a safety vest.

A good site visit builds trust. When you speak simple English, the client feels safe and informed. You show that Racional controls the schedule. You can say the project is ahead of schedule or explain a part that is behind schedule. This is the daily English of the construction site.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai usar frases-âncora para guiar o cliente: "Please follow me. Watch your step." e "Over here you can see the new slab."

Lembre também das duas frases de status: "This part is done." e "This area is still in progress."

lessons.title: Toolbox talks on safety
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conduzir um diálogo de segurança (toolbox talk) com a equipe, falando de riscos e do uso correto de EPI em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
A toolbox talk is a short safety meeting. It happens before the work starts. The team stands together for a few minutes. You talk about the hazards of the day. You talk about the risk and how to stay safe. At Racional, safety comes first on every site.

On a hyperscale data center for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, safety rules are very strong. Workers use PPE: a hard hat, gloves, and a harness. When a team is working at height, they must clip on the harness. A suspended load can be very dangerous. A wet floor is slippery. The team must know these risks.

A good safety briefing also asks people to report problems. A near miss is an accident that almost happened. When you report it, you stop the next one. North American clients love this culture. They see that Racional protects every worker, every day.
lessons.intro:
Na prática você vai usar frases-âncora de segurança: "Always wear your PPE." e "Clip on your harness when you work at height."

Lembre também: "Please report any near miss." e "The floor is slippery. Stay safe."
lessons.situation: Antes do início do turno, você reúne a equipe para um toolbox talk e revisa os principais riscos do dia diante do cliente norte-americano que acompanha a visita.
lessons.context: Good morning, team. Let's start our toolbox talk. Today we work at height on the third floor. Always wear your PPE. Clip on your harness. Look up for any suspended load. The floor is wet and slippery, so watch your step. Please report any near miss to me. Safety first. Let's stay safe today.

lessons.title: Stay in touch: keeping the relationship
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai manter o contato com o cliente entre as reuniões, usando frases simples para retomar conversa e cuidar do relacionamento.
lessons.overview:
A construction project can take 18 to 24 months. During all this time, the contract manager talks with the client many times. Between the formal meetings, there are small and warm moments. You stay in touch. You check in with the client. You ask "How did it go?" These small moments build a strong relationship.

North American clients like a friendly and open tone. After a long meeting, it is nice to catch up over a coffee. You can say "Let's grab a coffee" or "Talk soon!" When you reach out first, the client feels close to Racional. This trust helps when there is a hard problem on the site.

Good relationships are not only about the contract. They are about people. You can drop a line by email or message. You can say "say hi to your team". You can say "We look forward to the next visit". On a long data center project for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, this human side keeps the partnership warm and strong.
lessons.intro:
Aqui o tom é leve e pessoal. Você vai praticar frases para manter o contato: "Let's stay in touch." e "How did it go?"

Lembre também das despedidas amigáveis: "Talk soon!" e "We look forward to the next visit."
lessons.situation: Alguns dias depois de uma reunião, você escreve uma mensagem curta e amigável ao cliente norte-americano para manter o relacionamento aquecido durante o ciclo do projeto.
lessons.context: Hi John. It was great to see you last week. I just want to check in. How did the trip go? Let's stay in touch. Next time you are here, let's grab a coffee. Please say hi to your team. We look forward to your next visit. Talk soon!

lessons.title: Daily/weekly stand-ups
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai dar o seu status em um stand-up diário, dizendo o que está no prazo, o que está travado e o que precisa de atenção.
lessons.overview:
A stand-up is a short and fast meeting. It can be a daily meeting. The team stands and gives a quick update. Each person talks about their front of work. The goal is simple: share progress, show problems, and keep the project moving. At Racional, this rhythm keeps everyone aligned.

In your update, you say what is on track. You also flag a blocker. A blocker is a problem that stops the work. Maybe you are waiting on a supplier or a drawing. North American clients like this clear and honest style. You give a quick heads-up early, not too late.

On a fast data center project for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, the team uses stand-ups every day. You kick off the meeting and wrap up in a few minutes. You say "no blockers" when all is fine. You follow up after the meeting on open points. This habit protects the schedule and the cost.
lessons.intro:
Na prática você vai usar a estrutura do stand-up: "My front is on track." e "I have one blocker: I'm waiting on the supplier."

Lembre também: "No blockers from my side." e "I will follow up after the meeting."
lessons.situation: No stand-up diário com o time do cliente, você dá o seu status em poucas frases: o que avançou, o que está travado e o que você vai acompanhar depois.

lessons.title: Project closeout meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conduzir uma reunião de encerramento de obra, falando da entrega, da lista de pendências e da aprovação final do cliente.
lessons.overview:
A closeout meeting happens at the end of the project. The work is almost complete. Now Racional makes the handover to the client. You deliver the building. You show that the project is ready to use. This is a very important moment for the contract manager.

Before the final sign-off, the team checks a punch list. A punch list is a list of small things to fix. Each minor item must be done. When all outstanding points are closed, the client can approve the work. You also give the handover documents and the as-built drawings.

On a data center project for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, the closeout is very detailed. The client makes a final inspection. After the sign-off, the warranty period starts. A clean closeout shows that Racional delivers with quality and care. It opens the door for the next project.
lessons.intro:
Na prática você vai usar frases-âncora do encerramento: "The project is complete." e "We have a few minor items on the punch list."

Lembre também: "Here are the handover documents." e "Please sign off the final inspection."

lessons.context: Thank you all for coming. The project is now complete. Today we do the handover. We have a few minor items on the punch list. We will close them this week. lessons.title: Lessons-learned sessions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conduzir uma sessão de lições aprendidas, falando do que deu certo, do que melhorar e dos próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
A lessons learned session happens after the project. The team meets to review the work. You talk about what went well. You also talk about what to improve. The goal is to learn and to do better in the next project. At Racional, this habit makes every team stronger.

In the session, you look for the root cause of each problem. Maybe a long lead time from a supplier caused a delay. Maybe the procurement plan started too late. You capture each takeaway. You write a clear action item for the future. This is honest and practical work.

On a data center project for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, lessons learned are very valuable. North American clients respect this culture of improvement. You share the best practice with other teams. Going forward, Racional knows how to avoid the same problem. Each project makes the next one better.
lessons.intro:
Na prática você vai usar frases-âncora da sessão: "Let's review what went well." e "This is a clear action item."

Lembre também: "The root cause was a long lead time." e "Going forward, we will avoid this."

lessons.context: Let's start the lessons learned session. First, what went well. The safety culture was very strong. Now, room for improvement. The steel delivery was late. The root cause was a long lead time. So here is our action item: start procurement earlier. Going forward, we will avoid this delay. This is a good takeaway for the next project.

lessons.title: Hospital — pitch comercial
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você ensaia, em inglês, um pitch comercial completo para um cliente de hospital — com abertura, corpo (por que a Racional) e fechamento com convite — demonstrando domínio aplicado do curso.
lessons.overview:
A pitch is a short and clear talk. You use it to win a new client. As a contract manager at Racional, you give a pitch when a client wants to build a new hospital. The client is American, and the meeting is in English. Your job is simple. You show why Racional is the right partner.

A hospital is a hard project. The client is careful. He wants to hear three words: quality, safety, and reliability. So your pitch must show your strong track record. Racional has more than fifty years and more than six hundred projects. These numbers are your best argument. They build trust fast.

A good pitch has three parts. First, you introduce yourself with confidence. Then you say why Racional is strong — on time, on budget, and safe. At the end, you say your value proposition and you ask for the next step. This lesson is a capstone. You will practice the full pitch out loud, from start to finish.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE — uma apresentação conduzida por você, o gerente de contrato. O cenário é um pitch comercial para um cliente que quer construir um hospital.

Use três frases-âncora: a abertura "Thank you for your time. I'm Fernando, contract manager at Racional.", o corpo "We deliver hospitals on time, on budget, and safely." e o fechamento "We'd love to be your partner. Let's schedule a site visit."
lessons.situation: Você apresenta o pitch da Racional para a diretoria de um grupo hospitalar norte-americano que avalia construir um novo hospital no Brasil.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time. I'm Fernando, contract manager at Racional. We have over fifty years and more than six hundred projects. We build hospitals on time, on budget, and safely. Quality and safety are at the core of our work. We'd love to be your partner. Let's schedule a site visit.

lessons.title: Hospital — execução técnica & MEP críticos
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês, a execução técnica de um hospital para o cliente norte-americano — com foco nos sistemas críticos (MEP) e em como você garante segurança e continuidade.
lessons.overview:
A hospital is the hardest project at Racional. Many systems must work all the time. These are the critical systems. In English, we group them as MEP: mechanical, electrical, and plumbing. They keep people safe. They cannot fail.

Some systems are very important. The HVAC gives clean air and positive pressure in the operating room. This helps infection control. The backup generator gives power when the city power fails. The medical gas lines bring oxygen to the patients. We build redundancy, so there is always a second system.

In this capstone, you present these systems to an American client. The rule is simple. Do not just say "it works." Say how you proved it. For example: "We tested the generator under full load." Numbers and tests build trust. In a hospital, life safety always comes first.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE conduzida por você. O cenário é a entrega técnica de um hospital para um cliente norte-americano.

Use a estrutura de prova: nomeie o sistema ("The HVAC keeps positive pressure."), depois mostre o teste ("We tested the backup generator under full load.") e ligue à segurança ("Life safety comes first.").
lessons.situation: Visita técnica final ao hospital com o cliente americano e a equipe de comissionamento. Você conduz a apresentação dos sistemas críticos, sala por sala.
lessons.context: Good morning. Today I'll walk you through the critical systems. Let's start with the operating rooms. The HVAC keeps positive pressure and clean air at all times. We tested the backup generator under full load. It starts in ten seconds. The medical gas lines are pressure-tested and certified. Life safety comes first.

lessons.title: Data center — pitch comercial
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz, em inglês, o pitch comercial de um data center hyperscale para o cliente norte-americano — apresentando a Racional, o diferencial de prazo e a sua confiança para entregar.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a big building full of computers. Big tech clients build them — companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. When the client is hyperscale, the project is very large. Racional builds these. Now you give the pitch to win the new project.

This client wants three things. First, speed to market — the building must be ready fast. Second, a strong track record — proof that you did it before. Third, no surprises — you must deliver on time, every time. Racional has more than fifty years and over six hundred projects. This is your best argument.

A good pitch is short and full of numbers. You open with who you are. You show your competitive edge — speed. You say you can scale and ramp up the team fast. Then you ask for the next step. You are not selling concrete. You are selling trust to a reliable partner.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE conduzida por você. O cenário é o pitch comercial de um data center hyperscale para um grande cliente de tecnologia americano.

Use as frases-âncora do pitch de data center: "Racional has built for over fifty years.", "Speed to market is everything." e "We deliver on time, every time."
lessons.situation: Reunião comercial em São Paulo com a equipe de expansão de um cliente de tecnologia americano. Você apresenta a Racional como a construtora certa para o data center deles.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time. Racional has built for over fifty years. We have more than six hundred projects. For your data center, speed to market is everything. We deliver on time, every time. We've done hyperscale before, and we know how to scale fast. Speed is our competitive edge.

exercises.explanation: Um pitch forte é curto, cheio de números e termina deixando claro o seu diferencial. Confiança se transmite na voz.

lessons.title: Data center — execução, cooling & commissioning
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês, a execução técnica e a entrega de um data center — explicando o sistema de refrigeração (cooling) e o comissionamento (commissioning) que provam que tudo funciona.
lessons.overview:
After the pitch, you build the data center. Then you deliver it. Two topics matter most here. The first is cooling. The servers make heat. The cooling system keeps them cold. It must hold the target temperature, even at peak load. If the room is too hot, the computers stop. So cooling is life or death for a data center.

The second topic is commissioning. This is the test phase. You prove every system works before the client uses it. There are levels. Level 5 is the big one — an integrated systems test, with the full IT load running. The American client knows these words. Use the right name and the right number.

In this capstone, you lead the handover. You do not just say "we tested it." You say the level and the result: "We passed Level 5 with zero downtime." You give the test report. Then you say the words the client waits for: the data center is ready to go live.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE conduzida por você. Depois do pitch, chega a hora da entrega técnica do data center.

Use as frases-âncora da entrega: "The cooling system holds target temperature at peak load.", "We passed Level 5 with zero downtime." e "The data center is ready to go live."
lessons.situation: Reunião de handover do data center com o time de operações do cliente americano. Você apresenta os resultados do comissionamento e do sistema de refrigeração.
lessons.context: We're ready for handover. The cooling system holds the room within target temperature, even at peak load. We completed commissioning. We passed Level 5 with the full IT load running. There was zero downtime. Here is the test report. The data center is ready to go live.

exercises.explanation: Nível (Level 5) + condição (full IT load) + resultado (zero downtime). Essa tríade é a prova técnica que o cliente de data center espera.

exercises.prompt: Em 2 ou 3 frases, conte ao cliente o resultado do comissionamento e do cooling do data center. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (um sobre teste + um sobre refrigeração ou entrega). A correção olha apenas o uso dos termos.

exercises.modelAnswer: We're ready for handover. The cooling system holds the room within target temperature, even at peak load. We completed commissioning and passed Level 5 at full IT load, with zero downtime. The data center is ready to go live.
exercises.explanation: Resultado de teste + cooling estável + zero downtime: essa é a história que libera o data center para operar. Diga com confiança.

exercises.title: 3. Conduza o handover
exercises.targetText: We're ready for handover. The cooling system holds target temperature, even at peak load. We passed Level 5 commissioning at full IT load, with zero downtime. The data center is ready to go live.

lessons.title: Edifício corporativo — pitch comercial
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz, em inglês, o pitch comercial de um edifício corporativo (escritório) para o cliente norte-americano — vendendo qualidade, sustentabilidade (certificação) e experiência do usuário.
lessons.overview:
An office building sells something different. A hospital sells safety. A data center sells speed. An office sells image and experience. The client wants a building that people love. He wants a building that helps the company attract talent. Racional builds premium offices like this.

Three things matter in this pitch. First, green certification — for example, LEED. A green building uses less power. This means lower operating cost for the client. Second, quality finishes and natural light — a nice workspace for the people. Third, a smart building with good systems and well-being for the team.

The big idea is simple. Every technical word must become a business benefit. "LEED Gold" means "lower cost and a building people want to work in." You sell long-term value, not just walls. You open with the vision, you show the benefits, and you close with the value. And, of course, you build it on budget.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE conduzida por você. O cenário é o pitch comercial de um edifício corporativo para um cliente americano.

Use as frases-âncora do pitch de escritório: "We build offices that people love to work in.", "This design targets LEED Gold." e "That means lower energy costs and a healthier workspace."
lessons.situation: Reunião comercial com o cliente americano que vai construir a nova sede no Brasil. Você apresenta a Racional como a construtora que entrega um edifício corporativo de classe mundial.
lessons.context: Thank you for coming. We build offices that people love to work in. This design targets LEED Gold certification. That means lower energy costs and a healthier workspace. We use high-quality finishes, natural light, and smart systems. It is built on time and on budget. This is long-term value.

exercises.explanation: Num pitch de escritório, todo diferencial técnico vira benefício de negócio: LEED = custo menor + workspace melhor.

exercises.explanation: Abrir com a visão e ligar cada diferencial a um benefício de negócio é o que vende um edifício corporativo de alto padrão.

lessons.title: Edifício corporativo — entrega final & ROI
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês, a entrega final de um edifício corporativo para o cliente norte-americano — apresentando os resultados, o cumprimento de prazo e custo, e o retorno do investimento (ROI).
lessons.overview:
This is the final capstone of the course. You lead the final delivery of the office building. You hand over the new headquarters to the American client. Now you do not sell. Now you prove. You show the results, with numbers.

The client wants to hear three things. First, you delivered on time and on budget — you kept your promise. Even better, you came in under budget. Second, the quality is validated — you met the target. Third, the building makes money. This is the language of ROI — return on investment.

ROI is the bridge between the building and the business. The energy savings will pay back the green investment in a few years. This time is the payback. A green building also raises the asset value. You close the meeting with thanks and a hope for a long partnership. This is the top skill of a contract manager: connect the building to the client's money.
lessons.intro:
Esta é a aula CAPSTONE final do curso. Você conduz a entrega final do edifício corporativo e fala a língua do cliente americano: resultado de negócio e ROI.

Use as frases-âncora da entrega final: "We delivered on time and on budget.", "The energy savings will pay back the investment in five years." e "Here's to a long partnership."
lessons.situation: Cerimônia de entrega final da nova sede corporativa, com a diretoria do cliente americano presente. Você apresenta os resultados e o retorno do investimento.
lessons.context: It's my honor to hand over your new headquarters. We delivered on time and on budget. The building is LEED certified. The energy savings will pay back the green investment in five years. Quality is fully validated. Thank you for your trust. Here's to a long partnership.

exercises.prompt: Em voz alta, conduza a entrega final do edifício corporativo para a diretoria do cliente americano. Esta é a coroação do curso — fale com orgulho e firmeza.
exercises.explanation: A entrega final junta prazo, custo, qualidade e ROI numa fala curta e forte, e fecha com a parceria de longo prazo.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15 a 20 segundos, conduza a entrega final da sede corporativa: diga que entregou no prazo e no orçamento, mostre o retorno do investimento e feche agradecendo e abrindo a parceria futura. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can hand over the headquarters with pride.
I can say we delivered on time and on budget.
I can explain ROI and payback in simple English.
I can connect energy savings to the asset value.
I can close out the project and open a long partnership.

teacher.overview: M7 — Encerrar o curso com seis apresentações conduzidas pelo gerente de contrato dentro dos três cenários típicos da Racional, com clientes norte-americanos: hospital, data center e edi…

flow.how: Aluno organiza a apresentação; cheque tempo e estrutura.
Aluno conduz o cenário do início ao fim, em inglês.
Avalie clareza, fluência, vocabulário e domínio; grave.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Avaliar com critérios claros; gravar para devolutiva.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).

pill.tip: O sotaque 'neutro' do noticiário: claro, com o 'r' bem pronunciado. É o mais fácil de entender.
pill.sample: Let's go over the schedule and the next steps.
